## writeVideo
Write image arrays or movie frame structures to a VideoWriter.
Syntax: writeVideo(w, X)
Syntax: w.writeVideo(X)
Accepts H-by-W-by-3[-by-F] RGB, H-by-W[-by-1-by-F] grayscale or indexed arrays, or a 1-by-F struct array with cdata and colormap fields. Grayscale input to RGB profiles is replicated; indexed movie input is expanded through its colormap for RGB profiles. uint8 values are preserved. single and double intensities are clamped to [0,1], multiplied by 255 and rounded; indexed uint8 is zero based and indexed floating point is one based. Other classes, nonfinite pixels, invalid indices, changing dimensions and changing palettes are rejected. Indexed Colormap can come from the first movie frame. Output and scratch are admitted against evaluation limits; work polls cancellation between frames.
Example: file=[tempname '.avi']; w=VideoWriter(file,'Uncompressed AVI'); open(w); writeVideo(w,uint8(zeros(2,3,3))); close(w); delete(file)
Differences from MATLAB: writeVideo opens implicitly on a new handle as required by this native slice; MATLAB R2026b requires an explicit open. Floating intensities are clamped here. For native AVI, a write or property-setting error finalizes completed frames and closes the writer; for ffmpeg profiles it kills/reaps the encoder and discards the temporary file; an empty writer removes its temporary file. Deleting the handle also finalizes. Collecting the last native handle finalizes; collecting an external writer or dropping its engine kills the encoder and discards unpublished output. Finalization failure preserves the previous destination and removes the temporary file; errors on explicit close are reported, while destructor errors cannot be reported. Quality uses a square-root mapping to JPEG quantizer quality (75 maps to 87); JPEG bytes can differ across builds, which use image when available and a baseline JPEG fallback otherwise.

## dicomlookup
Look up an attribute in the current DICOM dictionary.
Syntax: name = dicomlookup(group,element); [group,element] = dicomlookup(name)
Use two numeric integer scalars (decimal, 0..65535) or two hexadecimal char/string scalars (1..4 digits). Names are case-sensitive. Missing tags return empty character text; missing names return two empty double matrices. The factory dictionary excludes odd private groups; custom dictionaries may name them. Exact tags take precedence over repeaters. Concrete repeaters reuse dicominfo field names: (6002,0010) is OverlayRows_2, (6000,0010) is OverlayRows_0. These concrete names round-trip; bare repeater keywords return the mask's zero-filled base tag.
Differences from MATLAB: non-base repeater suffixes are the project's documented uppercase hexadecimal convention. Uses one Engine's dictionary state; no process-wide dictionary or MATLAB search path. No byte-based VR inference.
Example: dicomlookup('0010','0010')   % PatientName
Example: [group,element] = dicomlookup('TransferSyntaxUID')

## dicomdict
Get or replace this Engine session's active DICOM dictionary.
Syntax: path = dicomdict('get'); dicomdict('set',filename); dicomdict('factory')
Factory lookup uses the compiled PS3.6 table. Get returns the file of the active dictionary: the canonical path given to set, or, while factory is active, a generated text copy of the compiled table (5299 rows) at <user cache folder>/matrust/dicom/<16 hexadecimal digits>/dicom-dict.txt on Linux (XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache), or <temporary folder>/matrust-dicom/<16 hexadecimal digits>/dicom-dict.txt on Windows and macOS. On Linux and other Unix systems except macOS, factory get errors if neither XDG_CACHE_HOME nor HOME supplies an absolute per-user cache folder. That copy is checked on every get and rewritten when missing or changed; it can be copied, edited and passed to set. Set validates and parses a text file once, then atomically replaces the current dictionary; failed sets preserve it. Relative paths use Current Folder. Factory restores the compiled table. dicominfo and dicomread use the active dictionary; their per-call 'Dictionary',filename option is parsed for that call only and leaves session state unchanged.
Text rows have four columns: (gggg,eeee) VR Keyword VM. Blank lines and # comments are allowed; hexadecimal tags may contain x wildcard nibbles, such as (60xx,0010). VRs use the PS3.5 codes; slash-separated alternatives (US/SS, OB/OW) preserve ambiguous factory VRs. VM accepts positive counts, ranges, n bounds and alternatives separated by ' or '. Keywords are 1..63 ASCII identifier characters starting with a letter. Duplicate tags and keywords are errors naming file and line; exact tags win over masks, and the most specific matching mask wins. A custom dictionary replaces factory naming and VRs, including private odd-group tags. Implicit private VR comes only from that dictionary; unknown primitive tags keep the existing skipped behavior.
Differences from MATLAB: factory get returns a generated copy in the user cache or temporary folder rather than a file shipped with the product; editing that copy changes nothing until it is passed to set, and the browser version has no file to return. Session state is per Engine; *_current actions are explicitly unsupported. Only text dictionaries are supported; MAT-format dictionaries error explicitly. Limits: 16 MiB input, 65536 entries, 1024 repeaters, 4096 bytes per line, and available engine memory. Parsing polls cancellation. Writer custom dictionaries and every dicomwrite Dictionary option are not supported yet; reset to factory before writing. No GUI or global path changes.
Example: dicomdict('factory')
Example: path = dicomdict('get')

## dicominfo
Read bounded metadata from a DICOM Part 10 file.
Syntax: info = dicominfo(filename); info = dicominfo(filename,'Dictionary',dictionaryFile)
Returns Filename, FileSize, Format ('DICOM'), available image dimensions and known public metadata. BitDepth uses BitsStored, falling back to BitsAllocated. Missing tags stay absent. Sequences are structs with Item_1, Item_2, ...; PN names have FamilyName, GivenName, MiddleName, NamePrefix and NameSuffix (optional Ideographic/Phonetic component structs). Numeric VRs retain their signed/unsigned integer or floating class and multiplicity as column vectors; DS/IS become double. Ordinary text removes right SPACE padding; UI removes right NUL padding. ASCII (default/ISO_IR 6) and ISO_IR 192 UTF-8 are supported, including inherited item character sets.
Differences from MATLAB: this bounded metadata slice supports Part 10 implicit VR little endian, explicit VR little endian, explicit VR big endian, Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian (1.2.840.10008.1.2.1.99), RLE Lossless (1.2.840.10008.1.2.5), JPEG Baseline Process 1 (1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.50) and JPEG Lossless Process 14 / Selection Value 1 (1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.57 / .70). Raw datasets, other transfer syntax UIDs, other character sets and options other than Dictionary error explicitly. dicominfo does not decode pixels; dicomread supports native grayscale/RGB and multiple frames. dicomwrite supports a bounded native grayscale, RGB and multiframe writer; dicomdict controls this Engine session; the app is not supported yet. The generated PS3.6 2026d public dictionary includes standard and retired data, file-meta and directory tags, including repeating tags; factory private tags and command elements are excluded. A custom text dictionary (dicomdict set or the Dictionary option) replaces naming and VRs for implicit and explicit files and may name private tags; tags it omits are skipped like unknown tags, except that SpecificCharacterSet is always read and counted against the metadata budget. Present known metadata fields use PS3.6 keywords; base overlay and curve fields use names such as OverlayRows_0 and CurveDimensions_0. Other base repeaters keep their keyword, and non-base repeaters append the wildcard value in uppercase hexadecimal. Explicit VR must belong to the dictionary VR set (UN remains skipped). Implicit US/SS pixel-related values use the nearest enclosing PixelRepresentation. For LUTDescriptor and the red, green and blue palette descriptors with VR SS, only the second value is signed; the first and third are unsigned, and dicominfo returns these mixed descriptors as int32 arrays. PixelData remains OW, and other ambiguous entries use the first listed VR. Unknown defined-length primitive tags are checked and skipped in this result; unknown implicit undefined-length values are unsupported. Native PixelData, FloatPixelData and DoubleFloatPixelData are skipped by checked file offsets; RLE and JPEG encapsulated PixelData items (Basic Offset Table, fragments, delimiter) are structurally checked by their lengths without reading fragment bytes; safely bounded metadata after pixels is inspected. Deflated files require inflating the entire dataset, including pixel bytes, even for dicominfo; this costs decoded-dataset memory and work, rather than metadata-only memory. Filename and FileSize describe the physical file and TransferSyntaxUID remains the original .99 UID. dicominfo and dicomread require regular files and reject FIFOs before opening them. Files are limited to 256 MiB; metadata uses a conservative 16 MiB budget capped by available engine memory, values to 1 MiB, structural nodes to 10000, sequence items to 1024 and parser nesting to 32. The existing engine struct depth/size limits additionally apply to the returned value. No writes are performed.
Example: exist('dicominfo','builtin')   % 5

## registrationEstimator
Open the desktop Registration Estimator to align a moving image with a fixed image and compare registration runs.
Syntax: registrationEstimator
Syntax: registrationEstimator(moving, fixed)
Example: try, registrationEstimator; catch err, disp(err.message); end
Requires the MatRust desktop; CLI calls report "registrationEstimator requires the desktop". moving and fixed are workspace variables holding H-by-W gray images (uint8, uint16, int16, single or double) or H-by-W-by-3 RGB images (uint8, uint16, single or double); RGB images are registered on their rgb2gray version and the registered image keeps its colour. Use sample data loads a synthetic pair (two Gaussian blobs at 0-255, moving = fixed under rigidtform2d(8,[6 -4])) and selects Rigid; Generate script then rebuilds that pair itself. Images can also be read from files, and optional imref2d variables place either image in world coordinates. Each Register press runs imregtform off the UI thread (cancellable) with the chosen technique (monomodal: MeanSquares and RegularStepGradientDescent; multimodal: MattesMutualInformation and OnePlusOneEvolutionary), transformation type (translation, rigid, similarity or affine), pyramid levels, maximum iterations, maximum step length or initial radius and optional initial transformation, then warps the moving image into the fixed frame with imwarp and OutputView. Every run is listed with its time and the normalized correlation of the registered and fixed images over the fixed frame; runs are kept until the images change. The view overlays fixed and moving or registered images with imfuse (falsecolor, blend, checkerboard or diff). Export writes the transformation, the registered image, its imref2d and the quality value of the selected run (existing names are replaced transactionally); Generate script saves the code that reproduces that run.
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D images only; no feature-based techniques, nonrigid (displacement field) registration, masks or session files.
Reference: https://www.mathworks.com/help/images/ref/registrationestimator-app.html

## dicomBrowser
Open the desktop DICOM Browser to scan folders, select image series, inspect frames and export data.
Syntax: dicomBrowser
Syntax: dicomBrowser(folder)
Requires the MatRust desktop; CLI calls report "dicomBrowser requires the desktop". Folder paths are resolved in Current Folder. Include subfolders is enabled initially. Scan and reads run off the UI thread and can be cancelled. Use sample data writes a synthetic DICOM folder with fullfile(tempdir,'matrust-dicom-sample') and scans that folder in the same cancellable job.
The browser exports the original typed volume in R-by-C-by-S-by-F layout, one dicominfo struct per file, and the full collection table. Window and level affect display only. Generated scripts scan again, select the series by SeriesInstanceUID, read every file in collection order, and concatenate frames along dimension four. Existing output variables are replaced transactionally.
Differences from MATLAB: folder input only; collection-table and DICOMDIR launch inputs, external viewer integrations and spatial reconstruction are not supported. Engine transfer-syntax and resource limits apply.
Reference: https://www.mathworks.com/help/images/ref/dicombrowser-app.html

## dicomCollection
Scan a DICOM folder or file and group series into a table.
Syntax: collection = dicomCollection(source); collection = dicomCollection(source,'IncludeSubfolders',tf)
Returns a table with one row per series (row names s1, s2, ...) and variables StudyDateTime, SeriesDateTime, PatientName, PatientSex, Modality, StudyDescription, SeriesDescription, StudyInstanceUID, SeriesInstanceUID, Rows, Columns, Channels, Frames and Filenames. Absent or invalid Gregorian dates and invalid times become NaT; an absent time on a valid date means midnight. TM accepts HH, HHMM or HHMMSS with optional 1-6 fractional digits after seconds. PS3.5 6.2 permits second 60 for a leap second; this engine returns NaT for it because fixed 86400-second datetime days cannot preserve a leap second. Frames sums NumberOfFrames across all files in each series, and Filenames holds a cell of string arrays sorted by InstanceNumber then filename. Non-DICOM files are skipped silently; DICOM files whose headers cannot be collected are skipped with warning dicomCollection:skipped. Retained text is capped in encoded bytes: UI 64, LO 64, PN 320 and descriptions 1024 (the LO cap also applies to LO descriptions); a longer field skips the whole file.
Differences from MATLAB: DICOMDIR input is not supported yet and errors explicitly. Scanning is bounded to 100000 files and 10000 distinct directories, stops at the first top-level pixel tag, and polls cancellation between files and during header reads. Files larger than 256 MiB are listed without reading native pixel payloads; deflated input decodes only the header with bounded compressed read-ahead. Header storage is capped at 16 MiB and the remaining memory budget. Nested pixel attributes are not supported and skip the file. File summaries, UID group indexes, paths, directory state and table construction are admitted against the remaining engine memory budget; exhaustion errors explicitly. Admission conservatively reserves 8 KiB plus path storage per candidate file, including skipped files, for the duration of a scan. Directory links are followed only within the canonical source root and duplicate canonical directories are scanned once; file symlinks use their opened target metadata. Native file I/O is unavailable in the browser.
Example: exist('dicomCollection','builtin')   % 5

## dicomread
Read grayscale or three-component DICOM pixels (native, deflated, RLE, JPEG Baseline/Lossless), including multiple frames.
Syntax: X = dicomread(filename); X = dicomread(info); X = dicomread(___,'Dictionary',dictionaryFile)
Returns raw stored samples as uint8/uint16 (grayscale or RGB) or int8/int16 (grayscale). Single-frame shapes are Rows-by-Columns for grayscale and Rows-by-Columns-by-3 for RGB; multiple frames return Rows-by-Columns-by-SamplesPerPixel-by-NumberOfFrames, retaining the singleton sample axis for grayscale. Only trailing singleton dimensions are trimmed. MONOCHROME1 and MONOCHROME2 values are unchanged: no rescaling, windowing, normalization or inversion. The scalar dicominfo struct form uses only its text Filename and reopens/revalidates the file. Relative filenames use Current Folder.
Differences from MATLAB: this bounded reader supports Part 10 implicit VR little endian, explicit VR little endian, explicit VR big endian and Deflated Explicit VR Little Endian (.99), using the same native pixel layouts after dataset inflation, plus RLE Lossless (1.2.840.10008.1.2.5) for the same grayscale/unsigned RGB types, single or multiple frames, plus 8-bit JPEG Baseline Process 1 (1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.50) in desktop builds. MONOCHROME1/2 requires SamplesPerPixel=1; RGB requires SamplesPerPixel=3 and PlanarConfiguration=0 (interleaved) or 1 (planar within each frame). Absent NumberOfFrames means 1; otherwise it must be a positive integer count. All frames are read. BitsAllocated must be 8 unsigned or 16 unsigned/signed; BitsStored must be 1 through BitsAllocated and HighBit=BitsStored-1. Unused bits are masked and signed stored samples are sign-extended. Only exact bytes for all samples and frames plus a single even-length padding byte when needed are accepted; individual native frames are not padded. Signed RGB, YBR, palette/indexed images, signed 8-bit, float, shifted-bit layouts, raw datasets, other compression/encapsulation (JPEG Extended 12-bit .51, JPEG-LS, HTJ2K .201-.203, video; RLE/JPEG writing; Extended Offset Tables), frame-selection and options other than Dictionary, and auxiliary outputs are not supported yet. A custom dictionary (dicomdict set or the Dictionary option) supplies the VRs of implicit files, so for those files it must list the pixel attributes dicomread needs (such as Rows, Columns and BitsAllocated). File admission is 256 MiB; engine dimension, evaluation and available workspace/scratch/output memory limits apply before pixel allocation. Deflated input requires a completed single raw RFC1951 stream (no zlib/gzip wrapper); exactly one trailing NUL is required when the compressed stream byte count is odd, and no trailing bytes are accepted when even. Missing/extra padding, concatenated streams and junk error. Decoded datasets are capped at 256 MiB and available engine memory before each capacity growth. Retained backing capacity, inflater/chunks, metadata, pixel scratch and typed output/transient copy all count against memory; engine work limits also bound inflation. RLE requires undefined-length OB PixelData with exactly one fragment per frame; an empty Basic Offset Table uses fragment order, a nonempty one must list every frame's fragment item offset. Each frame header must declare SamplesPerPixel*BitsAllocated/8 segments (MSB byte segment first per sample), first offset 64, strictly increasing offsets and zero unused entries. PlanarConfiguration must still be 0 or 1 for RGB but RLE segments are always by plane. PackBits runs may not cross a row or overfill/underfill a plane; -128 is a no-op; each segment must be even-length, with exactly one zero pad byte after an odd byte count and nothing else. Malformed tables, fragments, delimiters, segments or runs error. Offset table, one compressed frame, decoded planes and typed output/copy count against memory, and compressed bytes count as work, before decoding. JPEG Baseline is lossy: values are the decoder's reconstruction and can differ by a few levels from other decoders (checked against libjpeg-turbo within 1 level for grayscale and 3 for colour; in the last column or row of 4:2:2/4:2:0 colour frames whose size is even but not a multiple of 16, this decoder blends in padding samples and differences up to 8 levels were measured). It requires BitsAllocated=BitsStored=8 and PixelRepresentation=0. MONOCHROME1/2 return uint8 Rows-by-Columns unchanged; YBR_FULL_422 and YBR_FULL (SamplesPerPixel=3) are converted and returned as RGB uint8 Rows-by-Columns-by-3, while dicominfo still reports the stored PhotometricInterpretation; PlanarConfiguration must be present (0 or 1) but never reorders decoder output. PhotometricInterpretation RGB is accepted only when the stream itself signals untransformed RGB components (Adobe APP14 transform 0, or R,G,B component ids); an RGB header over an unmarked stream, a YBR header over an RGB-signalled stream, and other photometric values error. A frame may span several fragments: one frame with an empty Basic Offset Table concatenates all fragments; several frames need either a nonempty Basic Offset Table whose entries name each frame's first fragment item, or exactly one fragment per frame; frame boundaries are never guessed from JPEG markers. Every frame stream is validated before decoding: SOI first, one baseline SOF0 frame header with 8-bit precision and exactly Rows, Columns and SamplesPerPixel (extended, progressive, lossless and arithmetic frames are rejected), 1x1 grayscale or 4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 colour sampling, one interleaved scan whose every Huffman-coded block and restart marker is complete, then EOI and at most one zero pad byte. Truncated or corrupt streams, extra data and multi-scan streams error; no partial image is returned. One concatenated frame stream, decoder buffers, all decoded frames and typed output/copy count against memory, and compressed bytes count as work, before decoding; the decoder call for one admitted frame is not interruptible. Builds without the desktop/plot-export image decoder report the transfer syntax and the missing JPEG decoder; dicominfo still works there. Reads/inflation/parsing/decoding/conversion are cancellable; no writes are performed. The browser has no file access. Writing and the remaining DICOM batch are subsequent slices.
Example: exist('dicomread','builtin')   % 5

JPEG Lossless (.57 and .70) is available in every engine build, independently of the desktop decoder. It accepts SOF3 precision 2..16 equal to BitsStored, BitsAllocated 8 or 16, and one or three components with dimensions matching Rows/Columns. MONOCHROME1/2 return raw samples without inversion; RGB returns stored RGB; YBR_FULL returns stored Y/Cb/Cr without colour conversion (dicominfo keeps the stored PhotometricInterpretation). PixelRepresentation selects uint8/int8 or uint16/int16; signed samples use two's complement over BitsStored. Three-component data must be unsigned. Layout is R-by-C-by-S-by-F with trailing singleton dimensions removed, as for native reads. Both syntaxes share the baseline fragment/BOT rules and reject Extended Offset Tables. Process 14 accepts predictors 1..7; .70 requires predictor 1. Point transforms are restored once after decoding reduced samples. Only one interleaved scan with 1x1 component sampling is supported; nonzero restart intervals error explicitly because of the decoder's predictor-reset limitation. Complete entropy data, EOI and at most one zero pad byte are required; no partial image is returned. Compressed buffers, decoder workspace and output count against a 256 MiB peak cap and the remaining workspace budget. Cancellation is polled during validation, concatenation, decoder reads and conversion and between frames; reconstruction within one admitted frame is not interruptible. JPEG Extended .51, JPEG-LS and HTJ2K .201-.203 remain explicitly unsupported.

JPEG 2000 Part 1 (.90 lossless only and .91 reversible or irreversible) is available in every engine build. It accepts raw J2K codestreams with precision 1..16, BitsAllocated 8 or 16, one or three full-resolution components, signed or unsigned, and single or multiple frames. Output classes are uint8/int8/uint16/int16; dimensions are R-by-C-by-S-by-F with trailing singleton dimensions removed. MONOCHROME1/2 return raw samples without inversion; RGB with MCT disabled returns stored RGB. YBR_RCT with reversible MCT and YBR_ICT with irreversible MCT return decoder RGB. dicominfo reports PhotometricInterpretation unchanged from the file, including YBR_RCT/YBR_ICT. Metadata/MCT, size, component, precision, sign and sampling mismatches error. .90 requires reversible 5/3 with no quantization; JP2 box wrappers and partial images error. Fragment/BOT rules are shared with baseline/lossless JPEG; Extended Offset Tables remain unsupported. Packed packet headers (PPM/PPT) are explicitly unsupported. SIZ tile count is capped at 4096, decomposition levels at 16, quality layers at 1024 and total packets at 1048576; image, nominal tile, coding/precinct workspace, compressed buffers and typed output/copies must fit the remaining engine budget and a hard 256 MiB peak cap. Full resolution and all quality layers are decoded. Cancellation is checked during concatenation, validation, conversion and between frames; the decoder call for one admitted frame is not interruptible. Strict pure-Rust decoding is bounded before that call and decoder failures/panics become malformed-codestream errors. No JPEG 2000 writing is provided.


## dicomwrite
Write a native (uncompressed) grayscale, RGB or multiframe DICOM Part 10 file atomically.
Syntax: dicomwrite(X,filename); dicomwrite(X,filename,metadata); dicomwrite(X,filename,info,'CreateMode','copy'); dicomwrite(___,Name,Value)
X must be nonempty int8, int16, uint8 or uint16; values are preserved exactly. Shapes: R-by-C grayscale (MONOCHROME2, one sample per pixel); R-by-C-by-3 truecolor (uint8 or uint16 only: SamplesPerPixel 3, PhotometricInterpretation RGB, PlanarConfiguration 0, red, green and blue stored together for each pixel); R-by-C-by-1-by-F grayscale frames and R-by-C-by-3-by-F truecolor frames (NumberOfFrames F, all frames in one file). A 3-D array whose third dimension is not 3 errors and names the 4-D form; other ranks error. Signed classes are written as two's complement with PixelRepresentation 1. Rows, Columns, SamplesPerPixel, PhotometricInterpretation, PlanarConfiguration, NumberOfFrames, BitsAllocated, BitsStored, HighBit and PixelRepresentation are derived from X; supplied values must agree, and the derived values are what the file contains (PlanarConfiguration only for RGB, NumberOfFrames only for more than one frame). BitsStored equals BitsAllocated (8 or 16). Relative paths use Current Folder. Statement-only: requesting any output errors before writing.
Name/value options (names and text values are case-insensitive; a repeated option errors): TransferSyntax (UID), VR ('implicit' or 'explicit'), Endian ('ieee-le' or 'ieee-be'), CreateMode ('create', the default, or 'copy') and WritePrivate (logical, default false). The three native transfer syntaxes are explicit VR little endian (1.2.840.10008.1.2.1, the default), implicit VR little endian (1.2.840.10008.1.2) and retired explicit VR big endian (1.2.840.10008.1.2.2). VR and Endian choose among them; a given TransferSyntax overrides both; VR 'implicit' with Endian 'ieee-be' and no TransferSyntax errors. File meta is always explicit little endian. CompressionMode 'None', UseMetadataBitDepths false, MultiframeSingleFile true, ObjectType 'Secondary Capture Image Storage' and SOPClassUID 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.7 are accepted as their documented defaults and change nothing; any other value of these options errors as not supported yet and names the option.
Metadata must be one scalar struct. Allowed text fields: PatientName (DICOM PN text or the component struct returned by dicominfo), PatientID, StudyDate (empty or YYYYMMDD), StudyTime (empty or HH, HHMM, HHMMSS with optional 1-6 fractional second digits), Modality, StudyDescription, SeriesDescription, SOPClassUID, SOPInstanceUID, StudyInstanceUID and SeriesInstanceUID. SeriesNumber and InstanceNumber accept empty/text IS or a numeric signed 32-bit integer scalar. The derived numeric pixel fields accept real integer scalars; NumberOfFrames also accepts integer text. Text is VM=1, with VR length/format checks; NUL, control characters, backslash multiplicity and caller-supplied trailing space padding are rejected. PN permits up to three 64-character groups and five components per group. LO permits 64 characters. SpecificCharacterSet accepts empty/ISO_IR 6 (ASCII) or ISO_IR 192 (UTF-8); non-ASCII text automatically adds ISO_IR 192 when absent, and contradicting explicit ASCII declarations error.
Only Secondary Capture Image Storage SOPClassUID 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.7 is accepted. Missing SOPInstanceUID, StudyInstanceUID and SeriesInstanceUID are fresh OS-random UUIDv4 decimal 2.25 UIDs; explicit valid UIDs are preserved. File meta storage UIDs match the dataset. ImplementationClassUID is the stable deterministic UUID-derived 2.25.96426248368486820571789363904423688279 (derivation in tool/refs/dicom/SOURCES.md).
SC bookkeeping defaults: Modality OT, ConversionType WSD; empty PatientName, PatientID, PatientBirthDate, PatientSex, StudyDate, StudyTime, AccessionNumber, ReferringPhysicianName, StudyID, SeriesNumber, InstanceNumber and PatientOrientation when absent. These defaults do not constitute clinical IOD conformance or validation of arbitrary clinical metadata. In create mode recognized DICOM fields outside the create set and dicominfo bookkeeping fields are dropped silently, so dicomwrite(X,filename,dicominfo(source)) is accepted when the retained metadata agrees with X and the supported Secondary Capture subset. Unknown field names error and name the field; option names used as struct fields remain unsupported. Use CreateMode 'copy' to preserve other attributes.
CreateMode 'copy' takes the scalar struct dicominfo returns (or one built by hand) and writes every field that names an attribute of the factory dictionary, including repeating-group names such as OverlayRows_2, with the dictionary VR. Nothing is checked against an IOD and no missing value or UID is generated. Text VRs take a character vector or string scalar (several values separated by backslashes). DS and IS also take numeric arrays; DS is written as the shortest decimal that fits 16 bytes, so a double that needs an exponent keeps about 12 significant digits. PN takes text or the dicominfo struct form (FamilyName, GivenName, MiddleName, NamePrefix, NameSuffix, optional Ideographic and Phonetic structs, one struct element per name). US, SS, UL, SL, UV, SV, FL, FD and AT take numeric arrays (AT as 65536*group+element). OB, OW, OL, OV, OF, OD and UN take numeric arrays as raw cells. A sequence is a scalar struct with fields Item_1 ... Item_n, each a scalar struct, written with defined lengths. Attributes listed as US or SS follow PixelRepresentation of the written image, or of the enclosing item when it has one. For LUTDescriptor and the red, green and blue palette descriptors with VR SS, the first and third values are unsigned 16-bit integers and only the second is signed. Attributes that describe X always come from X, whatever the struct says: Rows, Columns, SamplesPerPixel, PhotometricInterpretation (MONOCHROME1 in the struct is kept for grayscale X), PlanarConfiguration, NumberOfFrames, BitsAllocated, BitsStored, HighBit, PixelRepresentation and PixelData. File meta (group 0002) is regenerated: TransferSyntaxUID from the written syntax, the MediaStorage UIDs from SOPClassUID and SOPInstanceUID, or from the struct's MediaStorageSOPClassUID and MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID when those are absent; with neither the call errors. Ignored silently: the dicominfo bookkeeping fields Filename, FileModDate, FileSize, Format, FormatVersion, Width, Height, BitDepth, ColorType and StartOfPixelData, every field whose name contains GroupLength, and other group 7FE0 fields. Private fields (Private_gggg_eeee and Private_gggg_eexx_Creator, hexadecimal) are dropped unless WritePrivate is true; then creators are written as LO and other private data as UN (numeric bytes or text), or with the VR the active custom dictionary gives that private tag. Any other field name errors and names the field. Text must be ASCII or, for LO, LT, PN, SH, ST, UC and UT, UTF-8 with SpecificCharacterSet ISO_IR 192 (added when absent). Copy limits: 16 MiB of serialized metadata, 1 MiB per value, 65534 bytes per short-VR value in the explicit syntaxes, 6 nested sequence levels, 1024 items per sequence and 10000 elements. Attributes with tags above PixelData are written after the pixels.
Rows and Columns are limited to 1..65535; all samples of all frames count against the existing engine element, evaluation and workspace budgets. In big endian only 16-bit samples are byte-swapped; an odd pixel byte count gets one trailing zero after the last frame. Create-mode serialized metadata is capped at 32 KiB and files at 256 MiB (admission reserves metadata headroom). Input, text projections, metadata and serialized output are admitted before encoding. Encoding (also between frames) and temporary writes poll cancellation. Validation or cancellation observed before atomic rename preserves an existing destination and removes the owned temporary file. Cancellation racing a successful rename cannot undo publication.
Differences from MATLAB: the default transfer syntax is explicit VR little endian (MATLAB: implicit), so the VR default is 'explicit'. Create mode builds only Secondary Capture and drops recognized attributes outside the listed create set; CT and MR objects and IOD checks are not supported yet. Copy mode needs a metadata struct, errors on field names that are not attributes and on option names used as struct fields (MATLAB accepts options as fields), always takes the pixel attributes from X (UseMetadataBitDepths true is not supported yet) and never writes compressed syntaxes (CompressionMode other than 'None' errors, also next to TransferSyntax). A wrong VR, Endian or CreateMode spelling errors even when TransferSyntax overrides the option. Private field names use the MathWorks dicominfo spelling, but this engine's dicominfo returns private fields only when a custom dictionary names them, so a plain round trip carries no private data. A custom session dictionary is read only for private-tag VRs with WritePrivate true; without it, and for every Dictionary option, the call errors as not supported yet; reset dicomdict to factory before writing. dicominfo charges each value 16 times against its 16 MiB budget, so it reads back about 1 MiB of metadata even though copy mode can write more. Multiframe X is always one file (MultiframeSingleFile false is not supported yet) and keeps the given SOPClassUID. Empty X errors instead of writing an empty image. Signed truecolor (int8/int16 R-by-C-by-3) errors as not supported yet. Indexed images, dicomwrite(X,cmap,filename), error as not supported yet. Classes outside the documented int8, int16, uint8 and uint16 (int32, uint32, int64, uint64, single, double, logical) error naming the class. This bounded engine slice does not support palette, compression or status outputs. Native file I/O is unavailable in the browser. This does not complete Engine 7a.
Example: exist('dicomwrite','builtin')   % 5


## readlines
Read lines of text file as a string array.
Syntax: lines = readlines(filename); lines = readlines(filename, Name, Value)
Returns a column string array. A trailing line ending does not add an empty last line. Supports WhitespaceRule ('preserve', 'trim', 'trimleading', 'trimtrailing'), EmptyLineRule ('read', 'skip', 'error'), LineEnding (default ["\n","\r\n","\r"]), and Encoding ('UTF-8', 'US-ASCII', 'ISO-8859-1', 'system'). LineEnding interprets escape notation such as "\n" and "\r\n"; readlines with "\r\n" also accepts lone CR and LF.
Example: writelines(["a"; "b"], "lines.txt"); lines = readlines("lines.txt")   % ["a"; "b"]
Differences from MATLAB: A trailing line ending does not add an empty last line. Text is bounded to 256 KiB per file and 65536 strings; UTF-16/UTF-32 encodings are not supported yet.

## writelines
Write text lines to a file.
Syntax: writelines(lines, filename); writelines(lines, filename, Name, Value)
Writes a string array, character array, or cell array of character vectors to filename, one line per element or row. Supports WriteMode ('overwrite' default, 'append'), LineEnding (default "\n" on all platforms), and Encoding ('UTF-8', 'US-ASCII', 'ISO-8859-1', 'system'). LineEnding interprets escape notation such as "\n" and "\r\n".
Example: writelines(["one"; "two"], "out.txt"); readlines("out.txt")   % ["one"; "two"]
Differences from MATLAB: LineEnding defaults to "\n" on all platforms; text is bounded to 256 KiB.

## ferror
File I/O error status for an open file identifier.
Syntax: msg = ferror(fid); [msg, errnum] = ferror(fid); ferror(fid, 'clear')
Returns the last error message and numeric error code for an open file identifier (empty and 0 when none). Passing 'clear' resets the stored error status.
Example: fid = fopen("f.txt", "w"); [msg, errnum] = ferror(fid); fclose(fid)
Differences from MATLAB: Standard identifiers 0, 1, 2 are rejected; only file identifiers from fopen are accepted.

## dos
Execute an operating system command.
Syntax: [status, cmdout] = dos(command); [status, cmdout] = dos(command, '-echo')
Runs command through the platform shell using the same engine path as system, returning exit status and captured output.
Example: [status, out] = dos("echo ok")
Differences from MATLAB: Runs on all operating systems via the same shell path as system.

## unix
Execute an operating system command.
Syntax: [status, cmdout] = unix(command); [status, cmdout] = unix(command, '-echo')
Runs command through the platform shell using the same engine path as system, returning exit status and captured output.
Example: [status, out] = unix("echo ok")
Differences from MATLAB: Runs on all operating systems via the same shell path as system.

## edit
Open a file or new buffer in the MatRust desktop editor.
Syntax: edit; edit name; edit file.m
Opens an existing file (resolved through the current folder and search path) in the desktop editor, or opens a new unsaved buffer if the file does not exist yet. Requires the MatRust desktop.
Example: edit notes.m
Differences from MATLAB: Only one file name per call is supported; errors in CLI and -batch modes.

## web
Open a web page in the system browser.
Syntax: web(url); web(url, '-browser'); stat = web(url)
Opens an http:// or https:// URL in the system browser when running in the MatRust desktop, or prints the URL in CLI mode. Other URL schemes are rejected.
Example: web("https://example.com")   % Open in a browser: https://example.com
Differences from MATLAB: Only http:// and https:// URLs and the '-browser' option are supported; the built-in MATLAB browser and toolbox documentation browser are not supported.

## waitfor
Wait for a dialog to close.
Syntax: waitfor(h)
For a headless message or progress dialog, returns immediately.
Example: h = waitbar(0); waitfor(h); close(h);
Differences from MATLAB: Only message and progress dialog handles are supported.

## listdlg
Select from a list in a dialog.
Syntax: [indx, tf] = listdlg('ListString', list, ...)
Options: 'ListString' (required cellstr, string array, or char array), 'SelectionMode' ('multiple' or 'single'), 'InitialValue' (1-based indices, default 1), 'PromptString', 'Name', 'OKString', 'CancelString', 'ListSize' ([width height]). Returns chosen indices indx and tf=1 on OK, or [] and tf=0 on Cancel. Needs the desktop app.
Example: [indx, tf] = listdlg('ListString', {'Red', 'Green', 'Blue'}, 'SelectionMode', 'single');
Differences from MATLAB: Legacy spacing options (uh, fus, ffs) are not supported.

## volumeViewer
Inspect and render 3-D volumes (desktop).
Syntax: volumeViewer
Syntax: volumeViewer(V)
Syntax: volumeViewer(V, 'VolumeType', 'Volume')
Syntax: volumeViewer close
Example: V = reshape(1:24, [3 4 2]); try, volumeViewer(V, 'VolumeType', 'Volume'); catch err, disp(err.message); end
Open the Volume Viewer desktop app with a nonempty real numeric or logical 3-D array, or open it empty to import data. Browse workspace volumes or grayscale DICOM series, or use the built-in Shepp–Logan sample. Rotate by dragging and zoom with the wheel. Adjust the rendering style, colormap, isosurface value, background and voxel spacing, and inspect XY, YZ and XZ slices. Export a settings struct to the workspace or generate a script and PNG of the viewport. Keep any companion MAT file beside the generated script. The command requires the MatRust desktop.

## pdeModeler
Solve 2-D elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic and eigenvalue PDEs (desktop).
Syntax: pdeModeler
Syntax: pdeModeler close
Example: try, pdeModeler; catch err, disp(err.message); end
Open the PDE Modeler desktop app to draw 2-D constructive solid geometry domains (Rectangle, Circle, Ellipse, Polygon, Select, Snap, Fit), edit shape coordinates and set formulas, decompose geometry into labelled edges, assign per-edge Dirichlet or Neumann boundary conditions, choose Elliptic, Parabolic, Hyperbolic, or Eigen PDE coefficients and mesh settings (Hmax, Linear/Quadratic), and run Mesh or Solve (with Cancel while running). Switch between the Draw, Geometry (pdegplot), Mesh (pdemesh), and Solution (pdeplot with Contour, Mesh overlay, and 3-D surface toggles) tabs; step through parabolic or hyperbolic time steps with the time slider and Play/Pause, or pick eigenmodes with λ shown. Use one-click samples (Plate with a hole, Heat in a plate), export model and results variables to the workspace, or generate a reproducible createpde script. The command requires the MatRust desktop.
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D scalar PDEs only; 3-D geometry and STL import, specialised models (structural, thermal, electromagnetic, femodel), adaptive mesh refinement (adaptmesh), and legacy assempde/initmesh/refinemesh/parabolic/hyperbolic workflows are out of scope. Parabolic and hyperbolic solves are refused above 4096 nodes x equations (increase Hmax). Boundary conditions are Dirichlet or Neumann only, on outer boundary edges. One coefficient set applies to all faces (no per-subdomain coefficients).

## arguments
Declare function input and output argument validation.
Syntax: arguments; name (dims) class {validators} = default; end
Syntax: arguments; opts.Name (dims) class {validators} = default; end
Syntax: arguments (Repeating); name (dims) class {validators}; end
Specifies size, class, validator functions, and default values for positional, name-value (`opts.Name`), repeating (`Repeating`), and output (`Output`) function arguments at the start of a function body. Name-value arguments accept `'Name', value` pairs, `Name=value` syntax, or a scalar struct, with case-insensitive unique partial name matching. Repeating arguments are validated per group and delivered as cell arrays.
Example: af([1 2], 'Scale', 3); function y = af(x, opts); arguments; x (1,:) double {mustBeNonnegative}; opts.Scale (1,1) double = 1; end; y = x * opts.Scale; end   % [3 6]
Differences from MATLAB: Package-qualified custom validator functions on the path follow standard function resolution.

## mustBePositive
Validate that value is positive.
Syntax: mustBePositive(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is not a real, positive number (or logical true).
Example: mustBePositive([1 2 3])
Differences from MATLAB: Duration inputs are not supported.

## mustBeNonnegative
Validate that value is nonnegative.
Syntax: mustBeNonnegative(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is not a real, nonnegative number or logical value.
Example: mustBeNonnegative([0 1 2])
Differences from MATLAB: Duration inputs are not supported.

## mustBeNegative
Validate that value is negative.
Syntax: mustBeNegative(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is not a real, negative number.
Example: mustBeNegative([-1 -2])
Differences from MATLAB: Duration inputs are not supported.

## mustBeNonpositive
Validate that value is nonpositive.
Syntax: mustBeNonpositive(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is not a real, nonpositive number.
Example: mustBeNonpositive([0 -1])
Differences from MATLAB: Duration inputs are not supported.

## mustBeNonzero
Validate that value is nonzero.
Syntax: mustBeNonzero(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is zero.
Example: mustBeNonzero([1 -2])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeFinite
Validate that value is finite.
Syntax: mustBeFinite(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is Inf, -Inf, or NaN.
Example: mustBeFinite([1 2 3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeNonNan
Validate that value is not NaN.
Syntax: mustBeNonNan(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is NaN.
Example: mustBeNonNan([1 Inf -Inf])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeInteger
Validate that value is an integer.
Syntax: mustBeInteger(A)
Throws an error if any element of A is not a finite real integer value.
Example: mustBeInteger([1 2 -3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeReal
Validate that value is real.
Syntax: mustBeReal(A)
Throws an error if A is complex.
Example: mustBeReal([1 2 3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeNumeric
Validate that value is numeric.
Syntax: mustBeNumeric(A)
Throws an error if A is not a numeric array.
Example: mustBeNumeric(int32([1 2]))
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeNumericOrLogical
Validate that value is numeric or logical.
Syntax: mustBeNumericOrLogical(A)
Throws an error if A is not numeric or logical.
Example: mustBeNumericOrLogical([true false])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeNonempty
Validate that value is not empty.
Syntax: mustBeNonempty(A)
Throws an error if A is empty.
Example: mustBeNonempty([1 2])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeMember
Validate that value is a member of a specified set.
Syntax: mustBeMember(A, S)
Throws an error if any element of A is not a member of S.
Example: mustBeMember(2, [1 2 3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeInRange
Validate that value is in a specified range.
Syntax: mustBeInRange(A, lower, upper); mustBeInRange(A, lower, upper, bounds)
Throws an error if any element of A is outside [lower, upper]. Optional bounds flag may be 'inclusive', 'exclusive', 'exclude-lower', or 'exclude-upper'.
Example: mustBeInRange([0 0.5 1], 0, 1)
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeGreaterThan
Validate that value is greater than another value.
Syntax: mustBeGreaterThan(A, c)
Throws an error if any element of A is not greater than c.
Example: mustBeGreaterThan([2 3], 1)
Differences from MATLAB: Only scalar real c is supported.

## mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual
Validate that value is greater than or equal to another value.
Syntax: mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual(A, c)
Throws an error if any element of A is less than c.
Example: mustBeGreaterThanOrEqual([1 2], 1)
Differences from MATLAB: Only scalar real c is supported.

## mustBeLessThan
Validate that value is less than another value.
Syntax: mustBeLessThan(A, c)
Throws an error if any element of A is not less than c.
Example: mustBeLessThan([0 1], 2)
Differences from MATLAB: Only scalar real c is supported.

## mustBeLessThanOrEqual
Validate that value is less than or equal to another value.
Syntax: mustBeLessThanOrEqual(A, c)
Throws an error if any element of A is greater than c.
Example: mustBeLessThanOrEqual([1 2], 2)
Differences from MATLAB: Only scalar real c is supported.

## mustBeText
Validate that value is text.
Syntax: mustBeText(A)
Throws an error if A is not a character vector, string array, or cell array of character vectors.
Example: mustBeText(["a" "b"])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeTextScalar
Validate that value is a single piece of text.
Syntax: mustBeTextScalar(A)
Throws an error if A is not a character vector or a scalar string.
Example: mustBeTextScalar("hello")
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeNonzeroLengthText
Validate that value is text with nonzero length.
Syntax: mustBeNonzeroLengthText(A)
Throws an error if A is not text or contains any zero-length text element.
Example: mustBeNonzeroLengthText("abc")
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeFile
Validate that value refers to an existing file.
Syntax: mustBeFile(A)
Throws an error if A is not text or any path does not name an existing file.
Example: writelines("hi", "a.txt"); mustBeFile("a.txt")
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeFolder
Validate that value refers to an existing folder.
Syntax: mustBeFolder(A)
Throws an error if A is not text or any path does not name an existing folder.
Example: mkdir("sub"); mustBeFolder("sub")
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeVector
Validate that value is a vector.
Syntax: mustBeVector(A); mustBeVector(A, 'allow-all-empties')
Throws an error if A is not a 1-by-n or n-by-1 vector (unless 'allow-all-empties' is passed and A is empty).
Example: mustBeVector([1 2 3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeRow
Validate that value is a row vector.
Syntax: mustBeRow(A)
Throws an error if A is not a 1-by-n row vector.
Example: mustBeRow([1 2 3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeColumn
Validate that value is a column vector.
Syntax: mustBeColumn(A)
Throws an error if A is not an n-by-1 column vector.
Example: mustBeColumn([1; 2; 3])
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeScalarOrEmpty
Validate that value is scalar or empty.
Syntax: mustBeScalarOrEmpty(A)
Throws an error if A is neither scalar nor empty.
Example: mustBeScalarOrEmpty(42)
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeA
Validate that value is of a specified data type.
Syntax: mustBeA(A, classNames)
Throws an error if A is not an instance of any class in classNames.
Example: mustBeA(int8(1), "numeric")
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## mustBeUnderlyingType
Validate that value has a specified underlying data type.
Syntax: mustBeUnderlyingType(A, types)
Throws an error if class(A) does not match any type in types.
Example: mustBeUnderlyingType(int8(1), "int8")
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## network
Neural network object created by feedforwardnet, fitnet, patternnet, cascadeforwardnet, selforgmap, narxnet, narnet or timedelaynet.
Syntax: net = feedforwardnet(hiddenSizes)
Syntax: y = net(x)
Holds layer sizes, weights, biases, transfer functions, data division settings and training configuration. Configure with configure(net, x, t), train with train(net, x, t), evaluate with net(x) or sim(net, x), and inspect weights with getwb and setwb.
Example: net = feedforwardnet(4); class(net)   % 'network'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports shallow feedforward, fitting, pattern-recognition, cascade-forward, self-organizing map and time-series networks; deep-learning DAG/dlnetwork layers are not supported yet.

## digitalFilter
Digital filter object returned by designfilt.
Syntax: d = designfilt(response, Name, Value)
Stores filter coefficients, second-order sections (for IIR designs), response type, impulse response, design method, sample rate and specification properties. Pass d directly to filter, filtfilt, freqz, impz, grpdelay, phasez and filtord.
Example: d = designfilt('lowpassfir', 'FilterOrder', 10, 'CutoffFrequency', 0.4); class(d)   % 'digitalFilter'
Differences from MATLAB: Only the response types and design methods supported by designfilt are represented; fvtool is not supported.

## digitalFilter.filter
Apply a designed digital filter to signal samples in forward order.
Syntax: y = filter(d, x)
Example: d = designfilt('lowpassfir', 'FilterOrder', 4, 'CutoffFrequency', 0.4); y = filter(d, [1 0 0 0 0 0])
See also: digitalFilter

## digitalFilter.freqz
Evaluate the complex frequency response of a designed digital filter.
Syntax: [h, w] = freqz(d, n)
Example: d = designfilt('lowpassfir', 'FilterOrder', 4, 'CutoffFrequency', 0.4); [h, w] = freqz(d, 8)
See also: digitalFilter

## digitalFilter.filtfilt
Filter a signal in both directions with a designed digital filter for zero phase shift.
Syntax: y = filtfilt(d, x)
Example: d = designfilt('lowpassfir', 'FilterOrder', 4, 'CutoffFrequency', 0.4); y = filtfilt(d, sin(0:0.2:6))
See also: digitalFilter

## LinearModel
Linear regression model returned by fitlm or stepwiselm.
Syntax: mdl = fitlm(X, y)
Holds fitted coefficients, R-squared, RMSE, degrees of freedom, sums of squares (SSE, SST, SSR), residuals, fitted values, formula, log-likelihood and information criteria. Call predict(mdl, Xnew) to evaluate predictions.
Example: mdl = fitlm([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8]); class(mdl)   % 'LinearModel'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports numeric matrix and table predictors with OLS fitting; robust fitting and interactive diagnostic plots are not supported yet.

## GeneralizedLinearModel
Generalized linear regression model returned by fitglm.
Syntax: mdl = fitglm(X, y, 'Distribution', dist)
Holds fitted coefficients, deviance, dispersion, R-squared, residuals, fitted values, formula, log-likelihood and information criteria for normal, binomial and Poisson families. Call predict(mdl, Xnew) to evaluate predictions.
Example: mdl = fitglm([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8]); class(mdl)   % 'GeneralizedLinearModel'
Differences from MATLAB: Uses IRLS with canonical and common link functions; custom link functions and offset vectors are not supported yet.

## ClassificationKNN
k-nearest neighbor classification model returned by fitcknn.
Syntax: mdl = fitcknn(X, Y)
Stores training predictors, class labels, neighbor count, distance metric and standardization state. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitcknn([0 0; 1 1; 2 2], [1; 1; 2]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationKNN'
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only; exhaustive search without KD-tree indexing.

## ClassificationTree
Decision tree classification model returned by fitctree.
Syntax: mdl = fitctree(X, Y)
Stores binary split nodes, class probabilities and predictor metadata. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss, crossval and predictorImportance.
Example: mdl = fitctree([0; 1; 2; 3], [1; 1; 2; 2]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationTree'
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only; surrogate splits and prune are not supported yet.

## ClassificationSVM
Support vector machine classification model returned by fitcsvm.
Syntax: mdl = fitcsvm(X, Y)
Stores support vectors, dual coefficients, bias, kernel settings and class names for binary classification. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitcsvm([-2; -1; 1; 2], [-1; -1; 1; 1]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationSVM'
Differences from MATLAB: Binary classification with linear, RBF and gaussian kernels (gaussian is RBF). Polynomial kernels, outlier fraction and custom kernel functions are not supported yet.

## ClassificationNaiveBayes
Naive Bayes classification model returned by fitcnb.
Syntax: mdl = fitcnb(X, Y)
Stores per-class feature distribution parameters and class priors. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitcnb([0; 0.2; 2; 2.2], [1; 1; 2; 2]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationNaiveBayes'
Differences from MATLAB: Gaussian ('normal') distributions on numeric predictors only. Kernel and multinomial ('mn') distributions are not supported yet.

## ClassificationDiscriminant
Discriminant analysis classification model returned by fitcdiscr.
Syntax: mdl = fitcdiscr(X, Y)
Stores class means, covariance estimate, discriminant type (linear or quadratic) and priors. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitcdiscr([0 0; 1 1; 3 3; 4 5], [1; 1; 2; 2]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationDiscriminant'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports linear and quadratic discriminant analysis on numeric predictors.

## ClassificationLinear
Regularized linear classification model returned by fitclinear.
Syntax: mdl = fitclinear(X, Y)
Stores linear weight vector, bias, learner type (logistic or SVM) and regularization strength. Evaluate with predict, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitclinear([-2; -1; 1; 2], [-1; -1; 1; 1]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationLinear'
Differences from MATLAB: Dense numeric predictors; binary classification only.

## ClassificationECOC
Multiclass error-correcting output codes classification model returned by fitcecoc.
Syntax: mdl = fitcecoc(X, Y)
Combines binary learners using a coding matrix for multiclass classification. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitcecoc([0; 1; 5; 6; 10; 11], [1; 1; 2; 2; 3; 3]); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationECOC'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports one-vs-one and one-vs-all coding with MatRust learner templates.

## ClassificationEnsemble
Boosted or bagged classification ensemble returned by fitcensemble.
Syntax: mdl = fitcensemble(X, Y)
Stores weak learners, learner weights and training metadata. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss, crossval and predictorImportance.
Example: mdl = fitcensemble([0; 1; 2; 3], [1; 1; 2; 2], 'Method', 'AdaBoostM1', 'NumLearningCycles', 5); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationEnsemble'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports AdaBoostM1, LogitBoost, GentleBoost and Bag methods on numeric predictors.

## ClassificationBaggedEnsemble
Bagged classification ensemble returned by fitcensemble with Method set to 'Bag'.
Syntax: mdl = fitcensemble(X, Y, 'Method', 'Bag')
Stores bootstrap-aggregated decision trees and in-bag indices. Supports oobLoss in addition to predict, resubLoss, loss, crossval and predictorImportance.
Example: mdl = fitcensemble([0; 1; 2; 3], [1; 1; 2; 2], 'Method', 'Bag', 'NumLearningCycles', 5); class(mdl)   % 'ClassificationBaggedEnsemble'
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only.

## ClassificationPartitionedModel
Cross-validated classification model returned by crossval.
Syntax: cvmdl = crossval(mdl, 'KFold', k)
Holds per-fold trained classifiers and partition indices. Fit the model first, then pass it to crossval with a k-fold or holdout partition. Evaluate out-of-fold predictions and loss with kfoldPredict and kfoldLoss.
Example: mdl = fitcknn([0; 0.1; 1; 1.1; 2; 2.1], [1; 1; 1; 2; 2; 2]); cv = crossval(mdl, 'KFold', 3); class(cv)   % 'ClassificationPartitionedModel'
Differences from MATLAB: fitcknn does not accept the inline 'CrossVal', 'on' option.

## RegressionTree
Decision tree regression model returned by fitrtree.
Syntax: mdl = fitrtree(X, y)
Stores binary regression split nodes and leaf means. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss, crossval and prune.
Example: mdl = fitrtree([1; 2; 3; 4], [1; 2; 3; 4]); class(mdl)   % 'RegressionTree'
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only; surrogate splits are not supported yet.

## RegressionSVM
Support vector machine regression model returned by fitrsvm.
Syntax: mdl = fitrsvm(X, y)
Stores support vectors, dual weights, bias and kernel parameters for epsilon-insensitive SVR. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitrsvm([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8]); class(mdl)   % 'RegressionSVM'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports linear, RBF and polynomial kernels on numeric predictors.

## RegressionGP
Gaussian process regression model returned by fitrgp.
Syntax: mdl = fitrgp(X, y)
Stores kernel hyperparameters, noise standard deviation and Cholesky factor for posterior mean and standard deviation prediction. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitrgp([1; 2; 3; 4], [1; 4; 9; 16]); class(mdl)   % 'RegressionGP'
Differences from MATLAB: Exact GP inference on bounded dataset sizes; sparse approximations are not supported yet.

## RegressionEnsemble
Boosted or bagged regression ensemble returned by fitrensemble.
Syntax: mdl = fitrensemble(X, y)
Stores regression tree learners and weights. Evaluate with predict, resubLoss, loss, crossval and oobLoss (for bagged ensembles).
Example: mdl = fitrensemble([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8], 'NumLearningCycles', 5); class(mdl)   % 'RegressionEnsemble'
Differences from MATLAB: Supports LSBoost and Bag on numeric predictors.

## RegressionLinear
Regularized linear regression model returned by fitrlinear.
Syntax: mdl = fitrlinear(X, y)
Stores linear coefficients, bias and regularization settings. Evaluate with predict, loss and crossval.
Example: mdl = fitrlinear([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8]); class(mdl)   % 'RegressionLinear'
Differences from MATLAB: Dense numeric predictors only.

## RegressionPartitionedModel
Cross-validated regression model returned by crossval.
Syntax: cvmdl = crossval(mdl, 'KFold', k)
Holds per-fold trained regression models and test-fold indices. Fit the model first, then pass it to crossval with a k-fold or holdout partition. Evaluate out-of-fold predictions and MSE with kfoldPredict and kfoldLoss.
Example: mdl = fitrtree([1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6], [1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6]); cv = crossval(mdl, 'KFold', 3); class(cv)   % 'RegressionPartitionedModel'
Differences from MATLAB: fitrtree does not accept the inline 'CrossVal', 'on' option.

## prob.NormalDistribution
Normal probability distribution object returned by makedist('Normal', ...) or fitdist(x, 'Normal').
Syntax: pd = makedist('Normal', 'mu', mu, 'sigma', sigma)
Stores mean mu and standard deviation sigma. Supports pdf, cdf, icdf, random, mean, std, var, median, paramci and negloglik.
Example: pd = makedist('Normal', 'mu', 0, 'sigma', 1); class(pd)   % 'prob.NormalDistribution'
Differences from MATLAB: Truncation via truncate() is not supported yet.

## prob.NormalDistribution.pdf
Evaluate the normal probability density at each value in x.
Syntax: density = pdf(pd, x)
Example: pd = makedist('Normal', 'mu', 10, 'sigma', 2); pdf(pd, [8 10 12])
See also: prob.NormalDistribution

## prob.NormalDistribution.cdf
Return the normal probability of a value less than or equal to each threshold in x.
Syntax: p = cdf(pd, x)
Example: pd = makedist('Normal', 'mu', 10, 'sigma', 2); cdf(pd, 10)
See also: prob.NormalDistribution

## prob.NormalDistribution.icdf
Find the normal quantile for each cumulative probability in p.
Syntax: x = icdf(pd, p)
Example: pd = makedist('Normal', 'mu', 10, 'sigma', 2); icdf(pd, [0.025 0.5 0.975])
See also: prob.NormalDistribution

## prob.NormalDistribution.random
Draw an m-by-n array of samples from a normal distribution.
Syntax: x = random(pd, m, n)
Example: pd = makedist('Normal', 'mu', 10, 'sigma', 2); random(pd, 2, 3)
See also: prob.NormalDistribution

## parallel.ThreadPool
Thread-based parallel pool object returned by parpool('Threads').
Syntax: p = parpool('Threads')
Exposes NumWorkers, Connected, Busy and IdleTimeout properties and accepts parfeval and delete.
Example: p = parpool('Threads'); class(p)   % 'parallel.ThreadPool'
Differences from MATLAB: Runs serially in MatRust with NumWorkers equal to 1.

## parallel.ProcessPool
Process-based parallel pool object returned by parpool or parpool('Processes').
Syntax: p = parpool
Exposes NumWorkers, Connected, Busy and IdleTimeout properties and accepts parfeval and delete.
Example: p = parpool('Processes'); class(p)   % 'parallel.ProcessPool'
Differences from MATLAB: Runs serially in MatRust with NumWorkers equal to 1.

## parallel.FevalFuture
Future object returned by parfeval.
Syntax: f = parfeval(@fn, nout, args...)
Stores the scheduled call result, state, error and metadata. Retrieve outputs with fetchOutputs or fetchNext and wait with wait. cancel leaves State as 'finished', and fetchOutputs still returns the value.
Example: f = parfeval(@sin, 1, 0); class(f)   % 'parallel.FevalFuture'
Differences from MATLAB: Executes eagerly and serially in MatRust; State is immediately 'finished'.

## parallel.job.CJSIndependentJob
Independent batch job object returned by batch.
Syntax: j = batch(@fn, nout, {args...})
Stores job state, ID and outputs. Retrieve outputs with fetchOutputs. load does nothing, because the job has already run. wait returns at once, and cancel leaves State as 'finished'.
Example: j = batch(@sin, 1, {0}); class(j)   % 'parallel.job.CJSIndependentJob'
Differences from MATLAB: Executes eagerly and serially in MatRust; remote cluster profiles are not supported.

## matlab.io.text.DelimitedTextImportOptions
Import options object for delimited text files returned by detectImportOptions.
Syntax: opts = detectImportOptions('file.csv')
Holds delimiter, header lines, data lines, variable names, variable types, selected variables and per-variable VariableOptions. Customize with setvartype, getvaropts and setvaropts, then pass to readtable, readtimetable, readmatrix, readcell or preview.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object supporting core CSV/TSV options; fixed-width and custom rule callbacks are not supported yet.

## matlab.io.spreadsheet.SpreadsheetImportOptions
Import options object for spreadsheet files returned by detectImportOptions.
Syntax: opts = detectImportOptions('file.xlsx')
Holds sheet selection, data range, variable names, variable types, selected variables and per-variable VariableOptions. Customize with setvartype, getvaropts and setvaropts, then pass to readtable, readtimetable, readmatrix, readcell or preview.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object supporting core XLSX import options; legacy XLS binary workbooks are not supported.

## matlab.io.NumericVariableImportOptions
Per-variable import options object for numeric columns returned by getvaropts or opts.VariableOptions.
Syntax: v = getvaropts(opts, varName)
Controls Name, Type, FillValue, TreatAsMissing, DecimalSeparator and ThousandsSeparator for a numeric table variable.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object; empty-field and error-rule callbacks are limited to built-in rules.

## matlab.io.TextVariableImportOptions
Per-variable import options object for char or string columns returned by getvaropts or opts.VariableOptions.
Syntax: v = getvaropts(opts, varName)
Controls Name, Type, FillValue, TreatAsMissing, WhitespaceRule, QuoteRule, Prefixes and Suffixes for a text table variable.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object. Prefixes and Suffixes strip matching text when the table is read.

## matlab.io.DatetimeVariableImportOptions
Per-variable import options object for datetime columns returned by getvaropts or opts.VariableOptions.
Syntax: v = getvaropts(opts, varName)
Controls Name, Type, InputFormat, DatetimeFormat, TimeZone and FillValue for a datetime table variable.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object; locale-specific month names are limited to English.

## matlab.io.DurationVariableImportOptions
Per-variable import options object for duration columns returned by getvaropts or opts.VariableOptions.
Syntax: v = getvaropts(opts, varName)
Controls Name, Type, InputFormat, DurationFormat and FillValue for a duration table variable.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object; supports standard h:m:s and scalar-unit duration formats.

## matlab.io.CategoricalVariableImportOptions
Per-variable import options object for categorical columns returned by getvaropts or opts.VariableOptions.
Syntax: v = getvaropts(opts, varName)
Controls Name, Type, Categories, Ordinal, Protected and FillValue for a categorical table variable.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object; supports core category list and ordinality properties.

## matlab.io.LogicalVariableImportOptions
Per-variable import options object for logical columns returned by getvaropts or opts.VariableOptions.
Syntax: v = getvaropts(opts, varName)
Controls Name, Type, FillValue, TrueSymbols, FalseSymbols and CaseSensitive for a logical table variable.
Differences from MATLAB: Value object. TrueSymbols and FalseSymbols are the texts read as true and false.

## registration.optimizer.RegularStepGradientDescent
Gradient-descent optimizer configuration object returned by imregconfig('monomodal').
Syntax: [optimizer, metric] = imregconfig('monomodal')
Holds GradientMagnitudeTolerance, MinimumStepLength, MaximumStepLength, MaximumIterations and RelaxationFactor for imregister and imregtform.
Example: [opt, ~] = imregconfig('monomodal'); class(opt)   % 'registration.optimizer.RegularStepGradientDescent'
Differences from MATLAB: Value object; used with 2-D intensity-based registration in imregister and imregtform.
