Evolutionary optimizer configuration object returned by imregconfig('multimodal').
Syntax: [optimizer, metric] = imregconfig('multimodal')
Holds GrowthFactor, Epsilon, InitialRadius and MaximumIterations for imregister and imregtform.
Example: [opt, ~] = imregconfig('multimodal'); class(opt)   % 'registration.optimizer.OnePlusOneEvolutionary'
Differences from MATLAB: Value object; used with 2-D intensity-based registration in imregister and imregtform.

## registration.metric.MeanSquares
Mean-squares similarity metric object returned by imregconfig('monomodal').
Syntax: [optimizer, metric] = imregconfig('monomodal')
Specifies mean squared intensity difference as the registration metric for imregister and imregtform.
Example: [~, met] = imregconfig('monomodal'); class(met)   % 'registration.metric.MeanSquares'
Differences from MATLAB: Value object for 2-D intensity-based registration.

## registration.metric.MattesMutualInformation
Mattes mutual-information metric object returned by imregconfig('multimodal').
Syntax: [optimizer, metric] = imregconfig('multimodal')
Holds NumberOfSpatialSamples, NumberOfHistogramBins and UseAllPixels for multimodal registration in imregister and imregtform.
Example: [~, met] = imregconfig('multimodal'); class(met)   % 'registration.metric.MattesMutualInformation'
Differences from MATLAB: Value object for 2-D intensity-based registration.

## cameraCalibrationErrors
Camera calibration standard-error object returned as the third output of estimateCameraParameters.
Syntax: [params, imagesUsed, errors] = estimateCameraParameters(imagePoints, worldPoints)
Exposes IntrinsicsErrors and ExtrinsicsErrors properties and supports displayErrors(errors, params).
Differences from MATLAB: Read-only value object for single-camera calibration; stereo calibration errors are not supported yet.

## intrinsicsEstimationErrors
Standard errors of estimated camera intrinsics, held in errors.IntrinsicsErrors.
Syntax: ie = errors.IntrinsicsErrors
Exposes SkewError, FocalLengthError, PrincipalPointError, RadialDistortionError and TangentialDistortionError.
Differences from MATLAB: Read-only value object produced by estimateCameraParameters.

## extrinsicsEstimationErrors
Standard errors of estimated camera extrinsics, held in errors.ExtrinsicsErrors.
Syntax: ee = errors.ExtrinsicsErrors
Exposes RotationVectorsError and TranslationVectorsError with one 3-element row per calibration pattern.
Differences from MATLAB: Read-only value object produced by estimateCameraParameters.

## Root
Graphics root object returned by groot.
Syntax: r = groot
Exposes screen and default-property queries such as ScreenSize, MonitorPositions, ScreenPixelsPerInch, Units, CurrentFigure, Children and ShowHiddenHandles.
Example: r = groot; numel(r.ScreenSize)   % 4
Differences from MATLAB: Single-monitor default geometry in headless mode; factory and default property overrides are limited to supported figure and axes properties.

## Root.set
Set a default property on the graphics root for new objects.
Syntax: set(r, property, value)
Example: r = groot; set(r, 'DefaultAxesFontSize', 14); get(r, 'DefaultAxesFontSize')
See also: Root

## Root.get
Read a property of the graphics root.
Syntax: value = get(r, property)
Example: r = groot; get(r, 'ScreenSize')
See also: Root

## Annotation
Figure-level annotation graphics object (line, arrow, doublearrow, textarrow, rectangle, ellipse) returned by annotation.
Syntax: h = annotation(type, x, y, Name, Value)
Stores normalized figure coordinates and appearance properties such as Color, LineWidth, LineStyle, HeadStyle, HeadLength, HeadWidth, FaceColor and FaceAlpha.
Differences from MATLAB: Normalized figure units only; subset of annotation properties supported.

## Text
Text graphics object returned by text, title, xlabel, ylabel or zlabel.
Syntax: t = text(x, y, str)
Holds String, Position, Color, FontSize, FontWeight, FontAngle, HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, Rotation and Interpreter properties.
Differences from MATLAB: Interpreter is tex, none or latex. latex renders a $...$ / $$...$$ math subset (fractions, sub/superscripts, Greek, \sqrt, \mathrm/\mathbf, \left/\right, \sum/\int and common symbols); unsupported syntax falls back to plain text.

## Text.set
Set a property of a text label.
Syntax: set(h, property, value)
Example: h = text(0, 1, 'Peak'); set(h, 'String', 'Maximum'); get(h, 'String')
See also: Text

## ColorBar
Colorbar graphics object returned by colorbar.
Syntax: c = colorbar
Holds Location, Limits, Label, Orientation, FontSize and Visible properties attached to an axes.
Differences from MATLAB: Ticks and TickLabels cannot be queried or set; ticks follow the colour limits.

## Image
Image graphics object returned by image, imagesc or imshow.
Syntax: im = imagesc(C)
Holds CData, XData, YData, CDataMapping and Visible properties inside an axes.
Differences from MATLAB: AlphaData is not a property of Image.

## Image.set
Set a property of an image.
Syntax: set(h, property, value)
Example: h = imagesc([1 2; 3 4]); set(h, 'CData', [4 3; 2 1]); get(h, 'CData')
See also: Image

## Volume
3-D volume graphics object returned by volshow.
Syntax: v = volshow(V)
Holds Data, RenderingStyle, Colormap, Alphamap, DataLimits, IsosurfaceValue, IsosurfaceColor, SlicePlaneValues, Transformation, Visible, OverlayData, OverlayRenderingStyle, OverlayColormap, OverlayAlphamap and OverlayDisplayRange properties.
Differences from MATLAB: Supports VolumeRendering, MaximumIntensityProjection, MinimumIntensityProjection, Isosurface and SlicePlanes; custom lighting shaders are not supported yet.

## SliceViewer
2-D orthogonal slice viewer graphics object returned by sliceViewer.
Syntax: s = sliceViewer(V)
Holds SliceNumber, SliceDirection, Colormap, DisplayRange, ScaleFactors, Parent, Visible and Tag properties for inspecting 3-D volume slices.
Differences from MATLAB: Supports X, Y and Z slice directions. Label overlays are not supported.

## OrthosliceViewer
Three-plane orthogonal slice viewer graphics object returned by orthosliceViewer.
Syntax: s = orthosliceViewer(V)
Holds SliceNumbers, CrosshairEnabled, Colormap, DisplayRange, ScaleFactors, Parent, Visible and Tag properties for synchronized XY, XZ and YZ slice views.
Differences from MATLAB: Synchronizes three orthogonal views inside a figure; interactive oblique reslicing is not supported yet.

## TiledChartLayout
Tiled chart layout graphics object returned by tiledlayout.
Syntax: t = tiledlayout(m, n)
Holds GridSize, TileSpacing, Padding, Title, XLabel, YLabel and Children properties for arranging axes created with nexttile.
Differences from MATLAB: Supports fixed grid and flow layouts; nested tiled layouts are not supported yet.

## TiledChartLayout.nexttile
Select the next free tile in a layout and return its axes.
Syntax: ax = nexttile(layout)
Example: layout = tiledlayout(1, 2); ax = nexttile(layout); plot(ax, 1:3)
See also: TiledChartLayout

## NumericRuler
Numeric axis ruler object exposed as ax.XAxis, ax.YAxis and ax.ZAxis.
Syntax: r = ax.XAxis
Holds Limits, LimitsMode, TickValues, TickValuesMode, TickLabels, TickLabelsMode, TickLabelRotation, TickLabelFormat, Exponent, Color and Label properties for an axis.
Differences from MATLAB: Scale, Direction and FontSize are not properties of NumericRuler. Use YLim and YColor for the right side of yyaxis.

## ConstantLine
Constant horizontal or vertical reference line object returned by xline or yline.
Syntax: h = yline(y)
Holds Value, Color, LineStyle, LineWidth, Label, LabelHorizontalAlignment, LabelVerticalAlignment and DisplayName properties.
Differences from MATLAB: Subset of label orientation and interpreter properties supported.

## Rectangle
2-D rectangle or rounded-rectangle graphics object returned by rectangle.
Syntax: r = rectangle('Position', [x y w h])
Holds Position, Curvature, FaceColor, EdgeColor, LineWidth and LineStyle properties.
Differences from MATLAB: Supports rectangular and curved corners in 2-D axes.

## Rectangle.set
Set a property of a rectangle.
Syntax: set(h, property, value)
Example: h = rectangle('Position', [0 0 2 1]); set(h, 'LineWidth', 2); get(h, 'LineWidth')
See also: Rectangle

## Patch
Polygon or triangulated surface patch graphics object returned by patch.
Syntax: p = patch(x, y, c)
Syntax: p = patch('Faces', F, 'Vertices', V)
patch(x, y, c) draws triangles or axis-aligned quadrilaterals and exposes Type, Parent, FaceColor, FaceAlpha, EdgeColor, EdgeAlpha, LineStyle, LineWidth, DisplayName and Visible. Faces and Vertices are not properties of that form. The indexed form requires triangular faces (three columns) and three-column Vertices; those objects also expose Faces, Vertices, FaceVertexCData and VertexNormals.
Differences from MATLAB: Indexed faces must be triangles. Quad meshes are not supported.

## Patch.set
Set a property of a patch.
Syntax: set(h, property, value)
Example: h = patch([0 1 0], [0 0 1], 'r'); set(h, 'FaceColor', 'blue'); get(h, 'FaceColor')
See also: Patch

## Patch.get
Read a property of a patch.
Syntax: value = get(h, property)
Example: h = patch([0 1 0], [0 0 1], 'r'); get(h, 'FaceColor')
See also: Patch

## VideoReader.hasFrame
Check whether another video frame is available to read.
Syntax: tf = hasFrame(v)
Syntax: tf = v.hasFrame()
Returns true while the VideoReader object v has unread frames remaining and false at end-of-stream.
Differences from MATLAB: Same behavior for supported MP4/AVI/MOV/MKV containers.

## VideoReader.readFrame
Read the next sequential video frame from a VideoReader object.
Syntax: frame = readFrame(v)
Syntax: frame = v.readFrame()
Syntax: frame = v.readFrame('native')
Returns top-down H-by-W-by-3 uint8 RGB, or H-by-W uint8 for grayscale, and advances v.CurrentTime. Indexed frames expand to RGB unless 'native' is requested. Native grayscale and indexed output is a struct with uint8 cdata and colormap (empty for grayscale).
Differences from MATLAB: See readFrame for supported containers and CurrentTime.

## VideoReader.read
Read a specific frame or range of frames from a VideoReader object.
Syntax: frame = read(v, index)
Syntax: frames = read(v, [startIndex endIndex])
Reads the requested 1-based frame index or inclusive range from the VideoReader object v.
Differences from MATLAB: Bounded by maximum frame count and memory limits.

## VideoReader.getFileFormats
List the video file extensions this installation can read.
Syntax: formats = VideoReader.getFileFormats()
Example: formats = VideoReader.getFileFormats(); formats(1).Extension
See also: VideoReader

## VideoWriter.open
Open a VideoWriter file for writing frames.
Syntax: open(v)
Syntax: v.open()
Choose a profile when creating v. The native profiles are 'Motion JPEG AVI' (default), 'Uncompressed AVI', 'Grayscale AVI' and 'Indexed AVI'. The 'MPEG-4', 'Motion JPEG 2000' and 'Archival' profiles require ffmpeg with a suitable encoder.
Differences from MATLAB: The destination file is published on close after frames have been written.

## VideoWriter.writeVideo
Append one or more image frames to an open VideoWriter object.
Syntax: writeVideo(v, img)
Syntax: v.writeVideo(img)
Writes an RGB or grayscale image frame (or 4-D stack of frames) to an open VideoWriter object v.
Differences from MATLAB: Frame dimensions must match across all writes to the same file.

## VideoWriter.close
Finalize and close an open VideoWriter file.
Syntax: close(v)
Syntax: v.close()
Flushes buffered frames and closes the output file associated with the VideoWriter object v. Close publishes the finished file in place of any existing destination. An open writer that received no frames leaves no file.
Differences from MATLAB: Replacement of an existing destination waits until close. An empty writer leaves no output file.

## VideoWriter.getProfiles
List the video encoding profiles available to VideoWriter.
Syntax: profiles = VideoWriter.getProfiles()
Example: profiles = VideoWriter.getProfiles(); profiles(1).Name
See also: VideoWriter

## imref2d.contains
Test whether world coordinates lie inside an imref2d spatial bounds.
Syntax: tf = contains(R, xWorld, yWorld)
Syntax: tf = R.contains(xWorld, yWorld)
Returns a logical array indicating which (xWorld, yWorld) points fall within R.XWorldLimits and R.YWorldLimits.
Example: R = imref2d([10 10]); R.contains(5, 5)   % true
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## imref2d.intrinsicToWorld
Convert intrinsic image coordinates to world coordinates using an imref2d object.
Syntax: [xWorld, yWorld] = intrinsicToWorld(R, xIntrinsic, yIntrinsic)
Syntax: [xWorld, yWorld] = R.intrinsicToWorld(xIntrinsic, yIntrinsic)
Maps intrinsic (column, row) coordinates to world (x, y) coordinates using R's pixel extents and limits.
Example: R = imref2d([10 10], 2, 2); [xw, yw] = R.intrinsicToWorld(1, 1);   % [2, 2]
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## imref2d.sizesMatch
Verify that an image's dimensions match an imref2d object's ImageSize.
Syntax: tf = sizesMatch(R, A)
Syntax: tf = R.sizesMatch(A)
Returns true when the first two dimensions of A equal R.ImageSize.
Example: R = imref2d([4 5]); R.sizesMatch(zeros(4, 5))   % true
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## imref2d.worldToIntrinsic
Convert world coordinates to intrinsic image coordinates using an imref2d object.
Syntax: [xIntrinsic, yIntrinsic] = worldToIntrinsic(R, xWorld, yWorld)
Syntax: [xIntrinsic, yIntrinsic] = R.worldToIntrinsic(xWorld, yWorld)
Maps world (x, y) coordinates to continuous intrinsic (column, row) coordinates.
Example: R = imref2d([10 10], 2, 2); [xi, yi] = R.worldToIntrinsic(2, 2);   % [1, 1]
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## imref2d.worldToSubscript
Convert world coordinates to rounded 1-based row and column subscripts.
Syntax: [I, J] = worldToSubscript(R, xWorld, yWorld)
Syntax: [I, J] = R.worldToSubscript(xWorld, yWorld)
Maps world (x, y) coordinates to integer pixel subscripts (row I, column J), returning NaN for out-of-bounds points.
Example: R = imref2d([10 10]); [I, J] = R.worldToSubscript(3, 2);   % I = 2, J = 3
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## affinetform2d.transformPointsForward
Apply a forward 2-D geometric transformation to points.
Syntax: [x, y] = transformPointsForward(tform, u, v)
Syntax: P = transformPointsForward(tform, U)
Transforms 2-D points forward using tform.A (premultiply convention for affinetform2d, rigidtform2d, simtform2d and transltform2d).
Example: t = affinetform2d([1 0 3; 0 1 4; 0 0 1]); [x, y] = t.transformPointsForward(1, 2);   % x = 4, y = 6
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D transformations only.

## affinetform2d.transformPointsInverse
Apply an inverse 2-D geometric transformation to points.
Syntax: [u, v] = transformPointsInverse(tform, x, y)
Syntax: U = transformPointsInverse(tform, P)
Maps output points back to input coordinates by solving the 2-by-2 linear part of tform.
Example: t = affinetform2d([1 0 3; 0 1 4; 0 0 1]); [u, v] = t.transformPointsInverse(4, 6);   % u = 1, v = 2
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D transformations only.

## affinetform2d.invert
Compute the inverse 2-D geometric transformation object.
Syntax: tinv = invert(tform)
Syntax: tinv = tform.invert()
Returns a transformation object of the same class representing the inverse mapping.
Example: t = affinetform2d([1 0 3; 0 1 4; 0 0 1]); tinv = t.invert(); tinv.A(1, 3)   % -3
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D transformations only.

## affinetform2d.outputLimits
Compute output world limits corresponding to input coordinate limits.
Syntax: [xLimitsOut, yLimitsOut] = outputLimits(tform, xLimitsIn, yLimitsIn)
Syntax: [xLimitsOut, yLimitsOut] = tform.outputLimits(xLimitsIn, yLimitsIn)
Transforms the bounding box [xLimitsIn, yLimitsIn] through tform and returns the enclosing output x and y ranges.
Example: t = affinetform2d([1 0 5; 0 1 0; 0 0 1]); [xo, yo] = t.outputLimits([0 10], [0 10]);   % xo = [5 15]
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D transformations only.

## affinetform2d.isRigid
Test whether a 2-D affine transformation is a rigid motion.
Syntax: tf = isRigid(tform)
Syntax: tf = tform.isRigid()
Returns true when the linear 2-by-2 part is orthogonal with determinant +1 within numerical tolerance.
Example: t = affinetform2d(eye(3)); t.isRigid()   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Uses a 1e-10 tolerance on the 2-by-2 matrix structure check.

## affinetform2d.isSimilarity
Test whether a 2-D affine transformation is a similarity transformation.
Syntax: tf = isSimilarity(tform)
Syntax: tf = tform.isSimilarity()
Returns true when the linear 2-by-2 part is a uniform scale times an orthogonal matrix, including reflections, within tolerance.
Example: t = affinetform2d([2 0 1; 0 2 0; 0 0 1]); t.isSimilarity()   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Uses a 1e-10 tolerance on the 2-by-2 matrix structure check.

## affinetform2d.isTranslation
Test whether a 2-D affine transformation is a pure translation.
Syntax: tf = isTranslation(tform)
Syntax: tf = tform.isTranslation()
Returns true when the linear 2-by-2 part equals the identity matrix within tolerance.
Example: t = affinetform2d([1 0 5; 0 1 -2; 0 0 1]); t.isTranslation()   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Uses a 1e-10 tolerance on the 2-by-2 matrix structure check.

## cameraIntrinsics.worldToImage
Project 3-D world points into 2-D image coordinates using cameraIntrinsics.
Syntax: imagePoints = worldToImage(intrinsics, R, t, worldPoints)
Syntax: imagePoints = intrinsics.worldToImage(R, t, worldPoints)
Projects N-by-3 world points through rotation R, translation t and the intrinsic matrix and lens distortion of intrinsics.
Example: intr = cameraIntrinsics([500 500], [320 240], [480 640]); p = intr.worldToImage(eye(3), [0 0 1], [0 0 0]);   % [320 240]
Differences from MATLAB: Accepts 3-by-3 rotation matrices and 1-by-3 translation vectors; rigidtform3d objects are not supported yet.

## cameraParameters.worldToImage
Project 3-D world points into 2-D image coordinates using cameraParameters.
Syntax: imagePoints = worldToImage(cameraParams, R, t, worldPoints)
Syntax: imagePoints = cameraParams.worldToImage(R, t, worldPoints)
Projects N-by-3 world points using the intrinsics and distortion stored in cameraParams together with pose (R, t).
Example: cp = cameraParameters('K', [500 0 320; 0 500 240; 0 0 1], 'ImageSize', [480 640]); p = cp.worldToImage(eye(3), [0 0 1], [0 0 0]);   % [320 240]
Differences from MATLAB: Accepts 3-by-3 rotation matrices and 1-by-3 translation vectors; rigidtform3d objects are not supported yet.

## cameraCalibrationErrors.displayErrors
Print camera calibration standard errors to the command window.
Syntax: displayErrors(errors, cameraParams)
Syntax: errors.displayErrors(cameraParams)
Formats and prints intrinsic and extrinsic parameter estimation uncertainties from a cameraCalibrationErrors object.
Differences from MATLAB: Prints plain-text summary lines; stereo calibration errors are not supported yet.

## cwtfilterbank.wt
Compute the continuous wavelet transform using a cwtfilterbank object.
Syntax: [cfs, f] = wt(fb, x)
Syntax: [cfs, f, coi] = wt(fb, x)
Evaluates the CWT of real signal vector x with the wavelet, sampling frequency, voices per octave and frequency limits configured in fb.
Example: fb = cwtfilterbank('SignalLength', 64); [cfs, f] = wt(fb, sin(linspace(0, 4*pi, 64))); size(cfs, 2)   % 64
Differences from MATLAB: Supports Morse, Amor and Bump wavelets on real 1-D signals; call as wt(fb, x).

## cwtfilterbank.freqz
Compute the frequency responses of the wavelets in a cwtfilterbank object.
Syntax: [psihat, f] = freqz(fb)
Returns the frequency-domain filter bank responses and corresponding frequency vector for fb.
Example: fb = cwtfilterbank('SignalLength', 64); [psihat, f] = freqz(fb); size(psihat, 2)   % 65
Differences from MATLAB: Supports Morse, Amor and Bump filter banks; call as freqz(fb).

## cwtfilterbank.wavelets
Compute the time-domain wavelets of a cwtfilterbank object.
Syntax: [psi, t] = wavelets(fb)
Returns the time-domain wavelet functions (one per scale) and time vector for fb.
Example: fb = cwtfilterbank('SignalLength', 64); [psi, t] = wavelets(fb); size(psi, 2)   % 64
Differences from MATLAB: Supports Morse, Amor and Bump filter banks; call as wavelets(fb).

## cwtfilterbank.scales
Return the wavelet scales of a cwtfilterbank object.
Syntax: s = scales(fb)
Returns the vector of scales derived from the wavelet, voices per octave and frequency limits of fb.
Example: fb = cwtfilterbank('SignalLength', 64); s = scales(fb); numel(s) > 0   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Call as scales(fb).

## cwtfilterbank.centerFrequencies
Return the center frequencies of the wavelets in a cwtfilterbank object.
Syntax: cf = centerFrequencies(fb)
Returns the center frequency of each wavelet scale in fb (in Hz when SamplingFrequency is set, or cycles/sample otherwise).
Example: fb = cwtfilterbank('SignalLength', 64, 'SamplingFrequency', 100); cf = centerFrequencies(fb); numel(cf) > 0   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Call as centerFrequencies(fb).

## cwtfilterbank.centerPeriods
Return the center periods of the wavelets in a cwtfilterbank object.
Syntax: cp = centerPeriods(fb)
Returns the center period of each wavelet scale in fb.
Example: fb = cwtfilterbank('SignalLength', 64); cp = centerPeriods(fb); numel(cp) > 0   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Always returns numeric periods, the reciprocals of the center frequencies. SamplingPeriod and PeriodLimits are not accepted; use SamplingFrequency and FrequencyLimits. Call as centerPeriods(fb).

## LinearModel.predict
Predict responses from a fitted LinearModel object.
Syntax: ypred = predict(mdl, Xnew)
Syntax: ypred = mdl.predict(Xnew)
Syntax: [ypred, yci] = predict(mdl, Xnew)
predict(mdl, Xnew) returns fitted values and, with two outputs, confidence intervals. The method form mdl.predict(Xnew) returns only the predictions.
Example: mdl = fitlm([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8]); mdl.predict(5)   % 10
Differences from MATLAB: Supports numeric matrix predictors and pointwise confidence intervals.

## GeneralizedLinearModel.predict
Predict responses from a fitted GeneralizedLinearModel object.
Syntax: ypred = predict(mdl, Xnew)
Syntax: ypred = mdl.predict(Xnew)
Syntax: [ypred, yci] = predict(mdl, Xnew)
predict(mdl, Xnew) returns mean predictions and, with two outputs, confidence intervals on the response scale. The method form mdl.predict(Xnew) returns only the predictions.
Example: mdl = fitglm([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8]); mdl.predict(5)   % 10
Differences from MATLAB: Supports numeric matrix predictors.

## ClassificationKNN.predict
Predict class labels and scores from a ClassificationKNN model.
Syntax: [label, score] = predict(mdl, Xnew)
Finds the k nearest training neighbors for each row of Xnew and returns predicted labels and posterior scores.
Example: mdl = fitcknn([0; 1; 5; 6], [1; 1; 2; 2]); predict(mdl, 0.5)   % 1
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only; call as predict(mdl, Xnew).

## ClassificationTree.predict
Predict class labels and scores from a ClassificationTree model.
Syntax: [label, score] = predict(mdl, Xnew)
Routes each row of Xnew down the fitted decision tree and returns predicted labels and leaf class probabilities.
Example: mdl = fitctree([0; 1; 5; 6], [1; 1; 2; 2], 'MinParentSize', 2); predict(mdl, 5.5)   % 2
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only; call as predict(mdl, Xnew).

## RegressionTree.predict
Predict numeric responses from a RegressionTree model.
Syntax: ypred = predict(mdl, Xnew)
Routes each row of Xnew down the fitted regression tree and returns leaf mean predictions.
Example: mdl = fitrtree([1; 2; 3; 4], [10; 10; 20; 20], 'MinParentSize', 2); predict(mdl, 3.5)   % 20
Differences from MATLAB: Numeric predictors only; call as predict(mdl, Xnew).

## cvpartition.training
Return logical indices for the training set of a cvpartition object.
Syntax: idx = training(c)
Syntax: idx = training(c, i)
Returns a logical column vector selecting training observations for holdout or fold i of k-fold cross-validation.
Example: c = cvpartition(10, 'KFold', 5); sum(training(c, 1))   % 8
Differences from MATLAB: Supports KFold, HoldOut, LeaveOut and Resubstitution partitions.

## cvpartition.test
Return logical indices for the test set of a cvpartition object.
Syntax: idx = test(c)
Syntax: idx = test(c, i)
Returns a logical column vector selecting test observations for holdout or fold i of k-fold cross-validation.
Example: c = cvpartition(10, 'KFold', 5); sum(test(c, 1))   % 2
Differences from MATLAB: Supports KFold, HoldOut, LeaveOut and Resubstitution partitions.

## cvpartition.repartition
Create a new random partition of the same type and size from a cvpartition object.
Syntax: c2 = repartition(c)
Returns a fresh cvpartition with the same partition settings and newly sampled fold assignments.
Example: c = cvpartition(10, 'KFold', 5); c2 = repartition(c); c2.NumTestSets   % 5
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## arima.estimate
Estimate parameters of an arima time-series model from observed data.
Syntax: [EstMdl, EstParamCov, logL] = estimate(Mdl, y)
Fits unknown AR, MA, constant and variance parameters of Mdl to series y by maximum likelihood.
Example: Mdl = arima(1, 0, 0); y = [0.2; 0.5; 0.3; 0.6; 0.4; 0.7; 0.5; 0.8; 0.6; 0.9]; est = estimate(Mdl, y); class(est)   % 'arima'
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Pass exogenous predictors as 'X'; they are estimated as Beta. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## arima.forecast
Forecast future values and conditional variances from an arima model.
Syntax: [YF, YMSE] = forecast(Mdl, numPeriods, 'Y0', Y0)
Computes minimum-MSE multi-step forecasts and forecast error variances from a fully specified arima model.
Example: Mdl = arima('Constant', 0, 'AR', {0.5}, 'Variance', 1); [yf, ymse] = forecast(Mdl, 3, 'Y0', [1; 2]); numel(yf)   % 3
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## arima.infer
Infer innovations and conditional variances of an arima model.
Syntax: [E, V, logL] = infer(Mdl, y)
Computes one-step-ahead residuals E, conditional variances V and log-likelihood logL for series y.
Example: Mdl = arima('Constant', 0, 'AR', {0.5}, 'Variance', 1); [e, v] = infer(Mdl, [1; 2; 1.5; 2.5]); numel(e)   % 4
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## arima.simulate
Simulate sample paths from an arima model.
Syntax: [Y, E, V] = simulate(Mdl, numObs)
Generates simulated observations, innovations and conditional variances from a fully specified arima model.
Example: Mdl = arima('Constant', 0, 'AR', {0.5}, 'Variance', 1); y = simulate(Mdl, 10); numel(y)   % 10
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## arima.summarize
Summarize an arima model.
Syntax: results = summarize(Mdl)
An estimated model returns a struct with Description, SampleSize, NumEstimatedParameters, LogLikelihood, AIC, BIC, Table and VarianceTable. An unestimated model returns the model itself.
Example: Mdl = arima('Constant', 0, 'AR', {0.5}, 'Variance', 1); s = summarize(Mdl); class(s)   % 'arima'
Differences from MATLAB: An unestimated model is returned unchanged. An estimated model returns a struct.

## garch.estimate
Estimate parameters of a garch, egarch or gjr conditional variance model.
Syntax: [EstMdl, EstParamCov, logL] = estimate(Mdl, y)
Fits unknown conditional variance parameters of Mdl to a return or residual series y by maximum likelihood.
Example: Mdl = garch(1, 1); y = [0.1; -0.2; 0.3; -0.1; 0.2; -0.3; 0.1; -0.2; 0.4; -0.1; 0.2; -0.1]; est = estimate(Mdl, y); class(est)   % 'garch'
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## garch.forecast
Forecast conditional variances from a garch, egarch or gjr model.
Syntax: VF = forecast(Mdl, numPeriods, 'Y0', Y0)
Computes multi-step conditional variance forecasts from a fully specified conditional variance model.
Example: Mdl = garch('Constant', 0.1, 'GARCH', {0.5}, 'ARCH', {0.2}); vf = forecast(Mdl, 3, 'Y0', [0.5; -0.4]); numel(vf)   % 3
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## garch.infer
Infer conditional variances and log-likelihood of a garch, egarch or gjr model.
Syntax: [V, logL] = infer(Mdl, y)
Computes the conditional variance path V and the log-likelihood logL for series y.
Example: Mdl = garch('Constant', 0.1, 'GARCH', {0.5}, 'ARCH', {0.2}); v = infer(Mdl, [0.5; -0.4; 0.3; -0.2]); numel(v)   % 4
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## garch.simulate
Simulate conditional variances and innovations from a garch, egarch or gjr model.
Syntax: [V, Y] = simulate(Mdl, numObs)
Generates simulated conditional variance and innovation paths from a fully specified conditional variance model.
Example: Mdl = garch('Constant', 0.1, 'GARCH', {0.5}, 'ARCH', {0.2}); [v, y] = simulate(Mdl, 10); numel(v)   % 10
Differences from MATLAB: Univariate series. Innovations are Gaussian or t.

## garch.summarize
Summarize a garch, egarch or gjr conditional variance model.
Syntax: results = summarize(Mdl)
An estimated model returns a struct with Description, SampleSize, NumEstimatedParameters, LogLikelihood, AIC, BIC and Table. An unestimated model returns the model itself.
Example: Mdl = garch('Constant', 0.1, 'GARCH', {0.5}, 'ARCH', {0.2}); s = summarize(Mdl); class(s)   % 'garch'
Differences from MATLAB: An unestimated model is returned unchanged. An estimated model returns a struct.

## cfit.confint
Compute confidence bounds on fitted coefficients of a cfit or sfit object.
Syntax: ci = confint(fitresult)
Syntax: ci = confint(fitresult, level)
Returns a 2-by-p matrix of lower and upper confidence limits for the fitted coefficients at the given confidence level (default 0.95).
Example: f = fit([1; 2; 3; 4], [2.1; 3.9; 6.1; 8.0], 'poly1'); size(confint(f))   % [2 2]
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## cfit.predint
Compute prediction or confidence bounds on fitted curve values of a cfit or sfit object.
Syntax: pi = predint(fitresult, x)
Syntax: pi = predint(fitresult, x, level, intopt, simopt)
Evaluates lower and upper functional or observation bounds at query points x.
Example: f = fit([1; 2; 3; 4], [2.1; 3.9; 6.1; 8.0], 'poly1'); size(predint(f, [2; 3]))   % [2 2]
Differences from MATLAB: Supports functional/observation and nonsimultaneous/simultaneous options for parametric fits.

## cfit.differentiate
Differentiate a fitted cfit curve or sfit surface.
Syntax: [fx, fxx] = differentiate(fitresult, x)
Evaluates first and optional second derivatives of the fitted curve at points x.
Example: f = fit([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8], 'poly1'); differentiate(f, 2)   % 2
Differences from MATLAB: Uses analytic derivatives for built-in library models and finite differences otherwise.

## cfit.integrate
Integrate a fitted cfit curve from a reference point.
Syntax: int = integrate(fitresult, x, x0)
Evaluates the definite integral of fitresult from x0 to each point in x.
Example: f = fit([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8], 'poly1'); integrate(f, 2, 0)   % 4
Differences from MATLAB: Curve fits (cfit) only.

## cfit.coeffvalues
Return the fitted coefficient values of a cfit or sfit object.
Syntax: vals = coeffvalues(fitresult)
Returns a row vector of fitted parameter values in the order of coeffnames(fitresult).
Example: f = fit([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8], 'poly1'); numel(coeffvalues(f))   % 2
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## cfit.coeffnames
Return the coefficient names of a fittype, cfit or sfit object.
Syntax: names = coeffnames(fitresult)
Returns a column cell array of coefficient names.
Example: f = fit([1; 2; 3; 4], [2; 4; 6; 8], 'poly1'); numel(coeffnames(f))   % 2
Differences from MATLAB: None.

## parallel.FevalFuture.fetchOutputs
Retrieve the outputs of a completed parallel.FevalFuture or batch job.
Syntax: [a, b, ...] = fetchOutputs(f)
Returns the outputs produced by the function passed to parfeval or batch.
Example: f = parfeval(@sin, 1, 0); fetchOutputs(f)   % 0
Differences from MATLAB: Futures complete eagerly in MatRust, so fetchOutputs returns immediately.

## parallel.FevalFuture.wait
Wait for a parallel.FevalFuture or batch job to reach a given state.
Syntax: wait(f)
Syntax: tf = wait(f, state, timeout)
Waits until future or job f reaches the requested state (default 'finished').
Example: f = parfeval(@sin, 1, 0); wait(f)
Differences from MATLAB: Futures complete eagerly in MatRust, so wait returns immediately.

## parallel.FevalFuture.cancel
Cancel a parallel.FevalFuture or batch job.
Syntax: cancel(f)
Does not change the future or job. State stays 'finished', and fetchOutputs still returns the value.
Example: f = parfeval(@sin, 1, 0); cancel(f); f.State   % finished
Differences from MATLAB: cancel is a no-op. The call has already run when the future or job is created.

## mpc.mpcmove
Compute one model predictive control move for an mpc controller and mpcstate object.
Syntax: [mv, info] = mpcmove(mpcobj, x, y, r)
Solves the MPC quadratic program at the current state x, measured output y and reference r, updating x in place and returning the manipulated variable move mv.
Example: p = ss(0.8, 1, 1, 0, 1); c = mpc(p, 1); x = mpcstate(c); mv = mpcmove(c, x, 0, 1); isscalar(mv)   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Linear time-invariant MPC without adaptive or LTV plant updates.

## mpc.sim
Simulate a closed-loop mpc controller over a sequence of reference samples.
Syntax: [y, t, u] = sim(mpcobj, T, r)
Runs T steps of closed-loop MPC simulation with reference trajectory r and returns plant outputs y, time vector t and manipulated variables u.
Example: p = ss(0.8, 1, 1, 0, 1); c = mpc(p, 1); [y, t, u] = sim(c, 5, ones(5, 1)); numel(t)   % 5
Differences from MATLAB: Linear time-invariant MPC simulation; Simulink-only options are not supported.
## mrUiFire
Test-only trigger that fires a UI component interaction and its callbacks synchronously.
Syntax: mrUiFire(h, action, args...)
Test-only MatRust helper (not a MATLAB function) for automated headless UI checks. Actions: 'press' (uibutton/pushbutton), 'type' (uieditfield/uispinner/uitextarea/edit), 'choose' (uidropdown/uilistbox/uiswitch/uiradiobutton/uibuttongroup/uitab/uitabgroup/popupmenu/listbox), 'slide' (uislider/slider), 'toggle' (uicheckbox/state uibutton/uiswitch/checkbox/togglebutton/radiobutton), 'edit' (uitable cell [r c], newValue), 'select' (uitable cell [r c]), 'cancel' (uiprogressdlg), and 'close' (uifigure).
Example: fig = uifigure; b = uibutton(fig, 'ButtonPushedFcn', @(s,e) set(s, 'Text', 'Done')); mrUiFire(b, 'press'); b.Text; delete(fig)
Differences from MATLAB: MatRust test-only helper; MATLAB uses matlab.uitest instead.

## guidata
Store or retrieve application data associated with a figure.
Syntax: guidata(h, data); data = guidata(h)
Associates arbitrary data with the figure containing handle h and retrieves it from any descendant handle or the figure itself.
Example: fig = figure('Visible', 'off'); guidata(fig, struct('count', 1)); d = guidata(fig); d.count; close(fig)
Differences from MATLAB: none for standard figure handle usage.

## cla
Clear axes.
Syntax: cla; cla('reset'); cla(ax); cla(ax, 'reset')
Deletes all graphics objects (lines, surfaces, images, text, legend) from the current or specified axes; 'reset' also resets axes properties to defaults.
Example: fig = figure('Visible', 'off'); ax = gca; plot(ax, 1:3, 1:3); cla(ax); numel(ax.Children); close(fig)
Differences from MATLAB: none for standard axes clearing.

## pde.PDEModel
2-D partial differential equation model handle object returned by createpde.
Syntax: model = createpde
Syntax: model = createpde(N)
Holds PDESystemSize, IsTimeDependent, Geometry, Mesh, EquationCoefficients, BoundaryConditions, InitialConditions and SolverOptions for a scalar or N-equation 2-D PDE workflow.
Example: m = createpde(2); class(m)   % 'pde.PDEModel'
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D general PDE models only; structural, thermal, electromagnetic and 3-D models are not supported.

## pde.AnalyticGeometry
2-D constructive solid geometry value object stored in a PDEModel's Geometry property.
Syntax: g = geometryFromEdges(model, dl)
Holds NumFaces, NumEdges, NumVertices and Vertices for a decomposed 2-D geometry matrix created with decsg or csgdel.
Example: m = createpde; g = geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); class(g)   % 'pde.AnalyticGeometry'
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D decomposed geometry matrices only; 3-D geometries and STL import are not supported.

## pde.FEMesh
2-D triangular finite-element mesh value object returned by generateMesh and stored in model.Mesh.
Syntax: mesh = generateMesh(model)
Syntax: mesh = generateMesh(model, Name, Value)
Holds Nodes, Elements, MaxElementSize, MinElementSize, MeshGradation and GeometricOrder for linear (3-node) or quadratic (6-node) 2-D triangular meshes.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); class(mesh)   % 'pde.FEMesh'
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D triangular meshes only; 3-D tetrahedral meshes are not supported.

## pde.StationaryResults
Stationary 2-D PDE solution object returned by solvepde.
Syntax: results = solvepde(model)
Holds NodalSolution, XGradients, YGradients and Mesh from a stationary elliptic PDE solve.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 0, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 1); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = solvepde(m); class(r)   % 'pde.StationaryResults'
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D meshes only; call interpolateSolution and evaluateGradient in function form.

## pde.TimeDependentResults
Time-dependent 2-D PDE solution object returned by solvepde with a time vector.
Syntax: results = solvepde(model, tlist)
Holds NodalSolution, SolutionTimes, XGradients, YGradients and Mesh from a parabolic or hyperbolic 2-D PDE solve.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 1); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); setInitialConditions(m, 0); r = solvepde(m, [0 0.1]); class(r)   % 'pde.TimeDependentResults'
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D meshes only; call interpolateSolution and evaluateGradient in function form.

## pde.EigenResults
2-D PDE eigenvalue solution object returned by solvepdeeig.
Syntax: results = solvepdeeig(model, range)
Holds Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues and Mesh for the eigenmodes found inside the requested eigenvalue interval.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 0); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = solvepdeeig(m, [0 50]); class(r)   % 'pde.EigenResults'
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D meshes only; call interpolateSolution in function form.

## matlab.apps.AppBase
Abstract handle superclass for App Designer and programmatic GUI apps.
Syntax: classdef MyApp < matlab.apps.AppBase
Provides registerApp, runStartupFcn and createCallbackFcn to bind an app instance to its UIFigure lifecycle and invoke private startup and component callback methods.
Example: ismember('handle', superclasses('matlab.apps.AppBase'))   % true
Differences from MATLAB: RunningAppInstance tracking, web apps, .mlapp saving and ComponentContainer authoring are not supported.

## Figure
Figure window graphics object returned by uifigure or figure.
Syntax: fig = uifigure
Syntax: fig = uifigure(Name, Value)
Holds Name, Position, InnerPosition, OuterPosition, Visible, Color, CloseRequestFcn, Number, NumberTitle, Tag, UserData, Children and Parent properties.
Example: fig = uifigure('Visible', 'off', 'Name', 'App'); fig.Name; delete(fig)
Differences from MATLAB: UI figures support a focused subset of window and callback properties; menu bars, toolbars and key/mouse callbacks are not supported yet.

## Figure.get
Read a property of a figure.
Syntax: value = get(f, property)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); get(f, 'Visible')
See also: Figure

## Figure.set
Set a figure property by name.
Syntax: set(f, property, value)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); set(f, 'Name', 'Trial 1'); get(f, 'Name')
See also: Figure

## Figure.close
Close the specified figure.
Syntax: close(f)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); close(f); isgraphics(f)
See also: Figure

## Figure.findall
Find graphics handles in a figure, including children with hidden handles.
Syntax: handles = findall(f, property, value)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); plot(1:3); lines = findall(f, 'Type', 'line'); numel(lines)
See also: Figure

## Figure.clf
Remove the plotted contents of a figure while keeping the figure open.
Syntax: clf(f)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); plot(1:3); clf(f); isgraphics(f)
See also: Figure

## Figure.movegui
Validate a screen placement request for a figure.
Syntax: movegui(f, position)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); movegui(f, 'center')
See also: Figure

## Figure.saveas
Save a figure to a file whose extension selects the output format.
Syntax: saveas(f, filename)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); plot(1:3); filename = [tempname() '.svg']; saveas(f, filename); delete(filename)
See also: Figure

## Figure.exportgraphics
Export a figure to a graphics file.
Syntax: exportgraphics(f, filename)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); plot(1:3); filename = [tempname() '.svg']; exportgraphics(f, filename); delete(filename)
See also: Figure

## Figure.print
Write a figure to a file in the graphics format selected by the device option.
Syntax: print(f, filename, device)
Example: f = figure('Visible', 'off'); plot(1:3); filename = [tempname() '.svg']; print(f, filename, '-dsvg'); delete(filename)
See also: Figure

Syntax: g = uigridlayout(parent, [m n])

## pde.PDEModel.geometryFromEdges
Attach a decomposed 2-D geometry matrix to a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: g = geometryFromEdges(model, dl)
Syntax: g = model.geometryFromEdges(dl)
Creates a pde.AnalyticGeometry from the decomposed geometry matrix dl, stores it in model.Geometry and returns it.
Example: m = createpde; g = m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); g.NumEdges   % 4
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D decomposed geometry matrices only; geometry cannot be replaced once a mesh exists on model.

## pde.PDEModel.pdegplot
Plot the 2-D geometry of a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: pdegplot(model)
Syntax: model.pdegplot(Name, Value)
Draws the boundary edges and optional EdgeLabels, FaceLabels and VertexLabels of model.Geometry.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); m.pdegplot('EdgeLabels', 'on'); close(gcf)

## pde.PDEModel.generateMesh
Generate a 2-D triangular finite-element mesh on a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: mesh = generateMesh(model)
Syntax: mesh = model.generateMesh(Name, Value)
Builds a linear or quadratic triangular pde.FEMesh from model.Geometry using optional Hmax, Hmin, Hgrad and GeometricOrder settings, and stores it in model.Mesh.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = m.generateMesh('Hmax', 0.5); size(mesh.Nodes, 2) > 0   % true
Differences from MATLAB: 2-D triangular meshes only.

## pde.PDEModel.pdemesh
Plot the finite-element mesh of a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: pdemesh(model)
Syntax: model.pdemesh(Name, Value)
Draws the mesh triangles stored in model.Mesh, with optional NodeLabels and ElementLabels.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); m.generateMesh('Hmax', 0.5); m.pdemesh(); close(gcf)

## pde.PDEModel.pdeplot
Plot a solution or mesh quantity on a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: pdeplot(model, Name, Value)
Syntax: model.pdeplot(Name, Value)
Plots scalar nodal data (XYData), contours (Contour), 3-D height (ZData), vector fields (FlowData) or mesh overlay on model.Mesh.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = m.generateMesh('Hmax', 0.5); m.pdeplot('XYData', mesh.Nodes(1, :)'); close(gcf)

## pde.PDEModel.specifyCoefficients
Assign PDE equation coefficients to a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: specifyCoefficients(model, 'm', m, 'd', d, 'c', c, 'a', a, 'f', f)
Syntax: assignment = model.specifyCoefficients('m', m, 'd', d, 'c', c, 'a', a, 'f', f, 'Face', faceIDs)
Sets the coefficients of the general second-order PDE m*u_tt + d*u_t - div(c*grad(u)) + a*u = f on all faces by default. Use 'Face' to assign coefficients to selected faces. Later assignments override earlier ones on the same face.
Example: m = createpde; a = m.specifyCoefficients('m', 0, 'd', 0, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 2, 'Face', 1); a.RegionID   % 1
Differences from MATLAB: 3-D 'Cell' regions are unsupported.

## pde.PDEModel.applyBoundaryCondition
Assign Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions to edges of a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: applyBoundaryCondition(model, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', edges, 'u', u)
Syntax: model.applyBoundaryCondition('neumann', 'Edge', edges, 'g', g, 'q', q)
In a mixed condition, 'u' and 'EquationIndex' constrain selected equations and 'g' and 'q' specify the Neumann condition on the remaining equations.
Example: m = createpde(2); bc = m.applyBoundaryCondition('mixed', 'Edge', 1, 'u', 0, 'EquationIndex', 1, 'g', [0; 1]); bc.EquationIndex   % 1
Differences from MATLAB: Only 2-D 'Edge' regions are supported.

## pde.PDEModel.setInitialConditions
Assign initial value and initial time derivative on a time-dependent pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: setInitialConditions(model, u0)
Syntax: model.setInitialConditions(u0, ut0)
Sets the initial solution u0 (and optional initial velocity ut0 for hyperbolic PDEs) on model.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); m.setInitialConditions(0); ~isempty(m.InitialConditions)   % true

## pde.PDEModel.solvepde
Solve a stationary or time-dependent 2-D PDE model.
Syntax: results = solvepde(model)
Syntax: results = model.solvepde(tlist)
Returns a pde.StationaryResults object for stationary problems or a pde.TimeDependentResults object when a time vector tlist is supplied.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); m.generateMesh('Hmax', 0.5); m.specifyCoefficients('m', 0, 'd', 0, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 1); m.applyBoundaryCondition('dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = m.solvepde(); max(r.NodalSolution) > 0   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Time-dependent solves are bounded at 4096 total degrees of freedom.

## pde.PDEModel.solvepdeeig
Solve a 2-D PDE eigenvalue problem on a pde.PDEModel.
Syntax: results = solvepdeeig(model, range)
Syntax: results = model.solvepdeeig(range)
Computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors in the interval range = [rmin rmax] and returns a pde.EigenResults object.
Example: m = createpde; m.geometryFromEdges(decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); m.generateMesh('Hmax', 0.5); m.specifyCoefficients('m', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 0); m.applyBoundaryCondition('dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = m.solvepdeeig([0 50]); numel(r.Eigenvalues) > 0   % true

## pde.AnalyticGeometry.pdegplot
Plot a pde.AnalyticGeometry object.
Syntax: pdegplot(g)
Syntax: g.pdegplot(Name, Value)
Draws the 2-D geometry edges stored in g with optional EdgeLabels, FaceLabels and VertexLabels.
Example: m = createpde; g = geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); g.pdegplot(); close(gcf)

## pde.FEMesh.findNodes
Find node indices in a pde.FEMesh matching a geometric query.
Syntax: ids = findNodes(mesh, 'box', xlim, ylim)
Syntax: ids = mesh.findNodes('radius', center, r)
Syntax: ids = mesh.findNodes('nearest', point)
Syntax: ids = mesh.findNodes('region', 'Edge', edges)
Returns 1-based node indices in mesh matching the box, radius, nearest-point or geometry-region query.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); ~isempty(mesh.findNodes('box', [0 0.5], [0 0.5]))   % true

## pde.FEMesh.findElements
Find element indices in a pde.FEMesh matching a geometric query.
Syntax: ids = findElements(mesh, 'box', xlim, ylim)
Syntax: ids = mesh.findElements('radius', center, r)
Syntax: ids = mesh.findElements('attached', nodeIDs)
Syntax: ids = mesh.findElements('region', 'Face', faces)
Returns 1-based triangle element indices in mesh matching the geometric, attached-node or face-region query.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); ~isempty(mesh.findElements('box', [0 0.5], [0 0.5]))   % true

## pde.FEMesh.pdemesh
Plot a pde.FEMesh object.
Syntax: pdemesh(mesh)
Syntax: mesh.pdemesh(Name, Value)
Draws the 2-D triangular elements of mesh with optional NodeLabels and ElementLabels.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); mesh.pdemesh(); close(gcf)

## pde.FEMesh.pdeplot
Plot nodal data on a pde.FEMesh object.
Syntax: pdeplot(mesh, Name, Value)
Syntax: mesh.pdeplot(Name, Value)
Plots scalar nodal fields, contours, 3-D height or vector fields defined on the mesh. For 'XYData', supply a numeric vector with one value per mesh node.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); mesh = generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); h = mesh.pdeplot('XYData', mesh.Nodes(1, :)'); get(h(1), 'Type'), close(gcf);   % 'patch'
Differences from MATLAB: Element-wise 'XYData' is unsupported.

## pde.StationaryResults.interpolateSolution
Interpolate a stationary PDE solution at query coordinates.
Syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq)
Syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq, equationIndex)
Evaluates the finite-element solution stored in results at points (xq, yq), returning NaN outside the mesh.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 0, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 1); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = solvepde(m); interpolateSolution(r, 0.5, 0.5) > 0   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Call as interpolateSolution(results, ...); dot-call syntax is not supported.

## pde.StationaryResults.evaluateGradient
Evaluate the spatial gradient of a stationary PDE solution at query coordinates.
Syntax: [gradx, grady] = evaluateGradient(results, xq, yq)
Syntax: [gradx, grady] = evaluateGradient(results, xq, yq, equationIndex)
Computes partial derivatives du/dx and du/dy of results at points (xq, yq).
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 0, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 1); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = solvepde(m); [gx, gy] = evaluateGradient(r, 0.25, 0.25); isfinite(gx) && isfinite(gy)   % true
Differences from MATLAB: Call as evaluateGradient(results, ...); dot-call syntax is not supported.

## pde.TimeDependentResults.interpolateSolution
Interpolate a time-dependent PDE solution at query coordinates and time indices.
Syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq, timeIndex)   % scalar PDE
Syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq, equationIndex, timeIndex)
With four arguments, a scalar PDE selects the requested time steps, while a system selects the requested equations at all time steps. With five arguments, argument four selects equations and argument five selects time steps.
Example: m = createpde(2); geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', [0; 2]); setInitialConditions(m, [0; 0]); r = solvepde(m, [0 0.5 1]); u = interpolateSolution(r, 0.25, 0.4, 2, 3); abs(u - 2) < 1e-10   % 1
Differences from MATLAB: Call as interpolateSolution(results, ...); dot-call syntax is not supported.

## pde.TimeDependentResults.evaluateGradient
Evaluate the spatial gradient of a time-dependent PDE solution at query coordinates.
Syntax: [gradx, grady] = evaluateGradient(results, xq, yq, timeIndex)   % scalar PDE
Syntax: [gradx, grady] = evaluateGradient(results, xq, yq, equationIndex, timeIndex)
With four arguments, a scalar PDE selects the requested time steps, while a system selects the requested equations at all time steps. With five arguments, argument four selects equations and argument five selects time steps.
Example: m = createpde(2); geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', [0; 2]); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); setInitialConditions(m, [0; 0]); r = solvepde(m, [0 0.5 1]); [gx, gy] = evaluateGradient(r, 0.25, 0.4, 2, 3); gx > 0 && gy > 0   % 1
Differences from MATLAB: Call as evaluateGradient(results, ...); dot-call syntax is not supported.

## pde.EigenResults.interpolateSolution
Interpolate PDE eigenmodes at query coordinates.
Syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq, modeIndex)   % scalar PDE
Syntax: u = interpolateSolution(results, xq, yq, equationIndex, modeIndex)
With four arguments, a scalar PDE selects the requested modes, while a system selects the requested equations at all modes. With five arguments, argument four selects equations and argument five selects modes.
Example: m = createpde(2); geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 0); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = solvepdeeig(m, [0 80]); u = interpolateSolution(r, 0.25, 0.4, [1 2], 3); numel(u)   % 2
Differences from MATLAB: Call as interpolateSolution(results, ...); dot-call syntax is not supported.

## pde.EigenResults.evaluateGradient
Evaluate the x and y derivatives of PDE eigenmodes at query points.
Syntax: [gx, gy] = evaluateGradient(r, xq, yq)
Syntax: [gx, gy] = evaluateGradient(r, xq, yq, index)
Syntax: [gx, gy] = evaluateGradient(r, xq, yq, equationIndex, modeIndex)
With one index argument, a scalar PDE selects modes and a system selects equations. With no indices, the result includes every equation and mode.
Example: m = createpde; geometryFromEdges(m, decsg([3;4;0;1;1;0;0;0;1;1])); generateMesh(m, 'Hmax', 0.5); specifyCoefficients(m, 'm', 0, 'd', 1, 'c', 1, 'a', 0, 'f', 0); applyBoundaryCondition(m, 'dirichlet', 'Edge', 1:4, 'u', 0); r = solvepdeeig(m, [0 50]); [gx, gy] = evaluateGradient(r, 0.25, 0.4, 1)
See also: pde.EigenResults

## matlab.apps.AppBase.registerApp
Register a UIFigure with a matlab.apps.AppBase subclass instance.
Syntax: registerApp(app, fig)
Links app and fig so closing or deleting fig deletes app, deleting app deletes fig, and a zero-output constructor keeps app alive while fig stays open.
Example: d = tempname; mkdir(d); addpath(d); writelines(["classdef RegMHelpApp < matlab.apps.AppBase","properties","UIFigure matlab.ui.Figure","end","methods","function app = RegMHelpApp","app.UIFigure = uifigure('Visible','off');","registerApp(app, app.UIFigure);","end","end","end"], fullfile(d, "RegMHelpApp.m")); a = RegMHelpApp; close(a.UIFigure); ~isvalid(a); rmpath(d); rmdir(d, 's')
Differences from MATLAB: Only registers uifigure handles; classic figure handles and RunningAppInstance tracking are not supported.

## matlab.apps.AppBase.runStartupFcn
Execute the startup function of a matlab.apps.AppBase subclass instance.
Syntax: runStartupFcn(app, @startupFcn)
Syntax: runStartupFcn(app, @(app)startupFcn(app, varargin{:}))
Invokes the startup function with access to private methods of app's class, deleting app if the startup function errors.
Example: d = tempname; mkdir(d); addpath(d); writelines(["classdef StartMHelpApp < matlab.apps.AppBase","properties","UIFigure matlab.ui.Figure","Ready logical = false","end","methods (Access = private)","function startupFcn(app)","app.Ready = true;","end","end","methods","function app = StartMHelpApp","app.UIFigure = uifigure('Visible','off');","registerApp(app, app.UIFigure);","runStartupFcn(app, @startupFcn);","end","end","end"], fullfile(d, "StartMHelpApp.m")); a = StartMHelpApp; a.Ready; delete(a); rmpath(d); rmdir(d, 's')

## matlab.apps.AppBase.createCallbackFcn
Wrap a matlab.apps.AppBase method as a UI component callback handle.
Syntax: cb = createCallbackFcn(app, @callbackFcn)
Syntax: cb = createCallbackFcn(app, @callbackFcn, requiresEvent)
Returns a function handle that calls callbackFcn(app, event) when requiresEvent is true, or callbackFcn(app) otherwise, with access to private methods of app's class.
Example: d = tempname; mkdir(d); addpath(d); writelines(["classdef CbMHelpApp < matlab.apps.AppBase","properties","UIFigure matlab.ui.Figure","Btn matlab.ui.control.Button","end","methods (Access = private)","function onPush(app, ~)","end","end","methods","function app = CbMHelpApp","app.UIFigure = uifigure('Visible','off');","app.Btn = uibutton(app.UIFigure);","app.Btn.ButtonPushedFcn = createCallbackFcn(app, @onPush, true);","registerApp(app, app.UIFigure);","end","end","end"], fullfile(d, "CbMHelpApp.m")); a = CbMHelpApp; isa(a.Btn.ButtonPushedFcn, 'function_handle'); delete(a); rmpath(d); rmdir(d, 's')

## audioplayer.play
Start asynchronous playback on an audioplayer object.
Syntax: play(p)
Syntax: p.play()
Syntax: play(p, start)
Syntax: play(p, [start finish])
Starts playback from sample 1 or the given 1-based sample index or inclusive [start finish] range and returns immediately.
Example: p = audioplayer(zeros(64,1), 8000); if isobject(p); p.play([1 16]); p.stop(); end

## audioplayer.playblocking
Play audio on an audioplayer object and wait until playback finishes.
Syntax: playblocking(p)
Syntax: p.playblocking()
Syntax: playblocking(p, start)
Syntax: playblocking(p, [start finish])
Blocks until playback of the clip or sample range completes, checking for cancellation.
Example: p = audioplayer(zeros(64,1), 8000); if isobject(p); p.playblocking(); end

## audioplayer.pause
Pause playback on an audioplayer object.
Syntax: pause(p)
Syntax: p.pause()
Suspends active playback on p at the current sample position so resume can continue it later.
Example: p = audioplayer(zeros(64,1), 8000); if isobject(p); p.play(); p.pause(); p.stop(); end

## audioplayer.resume
Resume paused playback on an audioplayer object.
Syntax: resume(p)
Syntax: p.resume()
In builds with audio support, isplaying(p) returns 1 while resumed playback is running.
Example: p = audioplayer(zeros(80000,1), 8000); if isobject(p); p.play(); p.pause(); p.resume(); disp(isplaying(p)); p.stop(); end   % 1
Differences from MATLAB: Null playback resumes at the paused sample. On an output device, the audible position depends on device buffering.

## audioplayer.stop
Stop playback on an audioplayer object.
Syntax: stop(p)
Syntax: p.stop()
Halts playback on p and resets CurrentSample to 1.
Example: p = audioplayer(zeros(64,1), 8000); if isobject(p); p.play(); p.stop(); end

## audioplayer.isplaying
Check whether an audioplayer object is currently playing.
Syntax: tf = isplaying(p)
Syntax: tf = p.isplaying()
Returns true while p is actively playing and false when stopped or paused.
Example: p = audioplayer(zeros(64,1), 8000); if isobject(p); p.isplaying(); end

## audiorecorder.record
Start asynchronous audio recording on an audiorecorder object.
Syntax: record(r)
Syntax: r.record()
Syntax: record(r, seconds)
Starts recording from the default audio input device into r and returns immediately; call stop(r) to end recording.
Example: r = audiorecorder(8000, 16, 1); if isobject(r); try, r.record(0.05); r.stop(); catch, end; end
Differences from MATLAB: Requires an available audio input device; ongoing recordings stop when the sample buffer limit is reached.

## audiorecorder.recordblocking
Record audio for a fixed duration on an audiorecorder object and wait until finished.
Syntax: recordblocking(r, seconds)
Syntax: r.recordblocking(seconds)
Records from the default audio input device for the given number of seconds, blocking until capture finishes.
Example: r = audiorecorder(8000, 16, 1); if isobject(r); try, r.recordblocking(0.05); catch, end; end
Differences from MATLAB: Requires an available audio input device.

## audiorecorder.stop
Stop recording on an audiorecorder object.
Syntax: stop(r)
Syntax: r.stop()
Ends an ongoing capture on r while keeping the samples already recorded.
Example: r = audiorecorder(8000, 16, 1); if isobject(r); r.stop(); end

## audiorecorder.getaudiodata
Return recorded audio samples from an audiorecorder object.
Syntax: y = getaudiodata(r)
Syntax: y = r.getaudiodata()
Syntax: y = r.getaudiodata(datatype)
Returns captured samples with one column per channel in double (default), single, int16, int8 or uint8 format.
Example: r = audiorecorder(8000, 16, 1); if isobject(r); y = r.getaudiodata(); size(y, 2); end

## audiorecorder.getplayer
Create an audioplayer object from an audiorecorder object's captured samples.
Syntax: p = getplayer(r)
Syntax: p = r.getplayer()
Returns a new audioplayer initialized with the audio currently stored in r and its sample format.
Example: r = audiorecorder(8000, 16, 1); if isobject(r); p = r.getplayer(); class(p); end

## delaunayTriangulation.pointLocation
Find the triangle containing each query point in a Delaunay triangulation.
Syntax: ID = pointLocation(DT, Q)
Syntax: [ID, B] = pointLocation(DT, Q)
Syntax: [ID, B] = DT.pointLocation(Q)
Locates each row [x y] of Q in DT.ConnectivityList, returning triangle row indices ID and optional barycentric coordinates B in each triangle's vertex order; points outside the triangulation return NaN.
Example: DT = delaunayTriangulation([0 0; 1 0; 0 1]); [id, b] = DT.pointLocation([0.25 0.25])
Differences from MATLAB: Accepts only an N-by-2 query matrix Q (separate x and y query vectors are not supported).

## delaunayTriangulation.nearestNeighbor
Find the closest vertex to each query point in a Delaunay triangulation.
Syntax: ID = nearestNeighbor(DT, Q)
Syntax: [ID, D] = nearestNeighbor(DT, Q)
Syntax: [ID, D] = DT.nearestNeighbor(Q)
Finds the nearest vertex in DT.Points to each row [x y] of Q, returning vertex indices ID and optional Euclidean distances D.
Example: DT = delaunayTriangulation([0 0; 1 0; 0 1]); [id, d] = DT.nearestNeighbor([0.1 0.2])
Differences from MATLAB: Accepts only an N-by-2 query matrix Q (separate x and y query vectors are not supported).

## delaunayTriangulation.edges
List the unique edges of a Delaunay triangulation.
Syntax: E = edges(DT)
Syntax: E = DT.edges()
Returns an M-by-2 matrix whose rows are sorted pairs of vertex indices into DT.Points for each unique edge in the triangulation.
Example: DT = delaunayTriangulation([0 0; 1 0; 0 1]); E = DT.edges()

## delaunayTriangulation.neighbors
Find the neighboring triangles of a Delaunay triangulation.
Syntax: N = neighbors(DT)
Syntax: N = DT.neighbors()
Returns an M-by-3 matrix where N(i, j) is the triangle adjacent to triangle i across the edge opposite vertex j, or NaN on the boundary.
Example: DT = delaunayTriangulation([0 0; 1 0; 1 1; 0 1]); N = DT.neighbors()
Differences from MATLAB: Triangle ID subset arguments (neighbors(DT, ti)) are not supported yet.

## delaunayTriangulation.convexHull
Find the convex hull boundary of a Delaunay triangulation.
Syntax: K = convexHull(DT)
Syntax: [K, A] = convexHull(DT)
Syntax: [K, A] = DT.convexHull()
Returns a closed counterclockwise column vector K of vertex indices into DT.Points tracing the convex hull, and optionally the enclosed area A.
Example: DT = delaunayTriangulation([0 0; 1 0; 0 1]); [k, a] = DT.convexHull()

## delaunayTriangulation.vertexAttachments
List the triangles attached to each vertex of a Delaunay triangulation.
Syntax: C = vertexAttachments(DT)
Syntax: C = DT.vertexAttachments()
Returns a column cell array with one cell per vertex in DT.Points containing ascending row indices into DT.ConnectivityList for the incident triangles.
Example: DT = delaunayTriangulation([0 0; 4 0; 1 3; 1.5 1]); C = DT.vertexAttachments()
Differences from MATLAB: Passing a vertex ID list (vertexAttachments(DT, vi)) is not supported yet.
